title.en: Volume 107 Biographies 32: Fu Yi, Lu Cai and son: Fang Yi, Chenzi Angfu: Wang Wujing, Zhao Yuan

sentences.zh: 傅弈傅弈，相州鄴人。

translations.literal: Fu Yi, Fu Yi, was a native of Ye in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yi was from Ye in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，以儀曹事漢王諒。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui, he served Prince Liang of Han as an aide in the Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: During Sui Kaihuang, he served Prince Liang Yang Liang in the ceremonial office.

sentences.zh: 諒反，問弈：「今茲熒惑入井，果若何？」

translations.literal: When Liang rebelled, he asked Yi: "This year Mars has entered the Well mansion—what will actually come of it?
translations.idiomatic: When Liang rose in rebellion, he asked Yi, "Mars has entered the Well this year—what does that portend?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「東井，黃道所由，熒惑之舍，烏足怪邪？

translations.literal: He replied: "The Eastern Well is where the Yellow Path passes and where Mars lodges—what is there to marvel at?
translations.idiomatic: Yi answered, "The Eastern Well lies on the ecliptic and is Mars's lodging—why treat that as strange?

sentences.zh: 若入地上井，乃為災。」

translations.literal: If it entered an earthly well, that would be a calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Only if it entered a well on earth would it spell disaster."

sentences.zh: 諒怒。

translations.literal: Liang grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was enraged.

sentences.zh: 俄及敗，弈以對免，徙扶風。

translations.literal: Soon Liang was defeated; Yi was spared because of his answer and was transferred to Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liang was defeated; Yi escaped punishment thanks to that reply and was reassigned to Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 高祖為扶風太守，禮之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was prefect of Fufeng, he treated Yi with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: While still prefect of Fufeng, the future Gaozu honored him.

sentences.zh: 及即位，拜太史丞。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Yi was appointed Vice Director of the Astro-calendrical Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After his accession, Yi was made Vice Director of the Astro-calendrical Bureau.

sentences.zh: 會令庾儉以父質占候忤煬帝死，懲其事，恥以術宦，薦弈自代。

translations.literal: It happened that the Director Yu Jian died because his father Zhi's divinations had offended Emperor Yang; mindful of this, he was ashamed to hold office by occult craft and recommended Yi to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The Director Yu Jian had died after his father Zhi's prognostications offended Emperor Yang; shamed by that precedent, Jian had refused to pursue a career through occult arts and recommended Yi as his successor.

sentences.zh: 弈遷令，與儉同列，數排毀之，儉不為恨。

translations.literal: Yi was promoted to Director and shared rank with Jian; he repeatedly slandered Jian, yet Jian bore no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yi rose to Director and served alongside Jian, often disparaging him, but Jian never held a grudge.

sentences.zh: 於是人多儉仁，罪弈遽且忿。

translations.literal: Thereupon many people praised Jian's kindness and blamed Yi as rash and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: People then widely praised Jian's forbearance and condemned Yi as hasty and spiteful.

sentences.zh: 時國制草具，多仍隋舊，弈謂承亂世之後，當有變更，乃上言：「龍紀、火官，黃帝廢之，《咸池》、《六英》，堯不相沿，禹弗行舜政，周弗襲湯禮。

translations.literal: At that time the state institutions were being drafted and largely followed Sui usage; Yi held that after inheriting a chaotic age there ought to be change, and submitted a memorial: "The Dragon Era and the Fire Office—Huangdi abolished them; 'Xianchi' and 'Liuying'—Yao did not continue them; Yu did not carry out Shun's policies, and Zhou did not inherit Tang's rites.
translations.idiomatic: State institutions were then being drafted, mostly along Sui lines; Yi argued that after a age of turmoil reforms were due and memorialized: "Huangdi discarded the Dragon Era and Fire Office; Yao did not perpetuate 'Xianchi' and 'Liuying'; Yu did not follow Shun's government, and Zhou did not adopt Tang's ritual code.

sentences.zh: 《易》稱'巳日乃孚，革而信也'，故曰'革之時大矣哉'。

translations.literal: The Changes says, 'On the si day there is truth; revolution and faith,' and therefore says, 'How great is the time of revolution!'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "On the si day faith is won—revolution brings trust," and therefore declares, "How momentous is the season of reform!"

sentences.zh: 有隋之季，違天害民，專峻刑法，殺戮賢俊，天下兆庶同心叛之。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui, it defied Heaven and harmed the people, relied exclusively on harsh penal law, slaughtered worthy men, and all the myriad commoners of the realm turned against it as one.
translations.idiomatic: Late Sui defied Heaven, harmed the people, leaned on brutal law, and killed the worthy until the whole realm rose against it as one.

sentences.zh: 陛下撥亂反正，而官名、律令一用隋舊。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has quelled disorder and restored order, yet office titles and statutes still wholly employ Sui's old forms.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has restored order after chaos, yet offices and statutes still follow Sui wholesale.

sentences.zh: 且懲沸羹者吹冷齏，傷弓之鳥驚曲木，況天下久苦隋暴，安得不新其耳目哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, one who has been scalded by boiling broth blows on cold pickles; a bird wounded by the bow startles at bent wood—how much more, when the realm has long suffered Sui's tyranny, can it fail to refresh its eyes and ears?
translations.idiomatic: A man scalded by boiling broth will blow on cold pickles; a bird once struck by an arrow flinches at bent wood—after so long under Sui's cruelty, how could the realm not crave something new to see and hear?

sentences.zh: 改正朔，易服色，變律令，革官名，功極作樂，治終制禮，使民知盛德之隆，此其時也。

translations.literal: Correct the calendar, change ceremonial colors, alter statutes, reform office names; when merit reaches its height compose music, when governance is complete institute rites—let the people know how lofty your flourishing virtue is: this is the time.
translations.idiomatic: Revise the calendar, change ritual colors, rewrite laws, rename offices; when achievement is complete, compose music, and when rule is settled, fix the rites—so the people may know how grand your virtue has become. That moment is now.

sentences.zh: 然官貴簡約，夏後官百不如虞氏五十，週三百不如商之百。」

translations.literal: Yet offices should value simplicity: Xia's hundred posts were fewer than Shun's fifty, and Zhou's three hundred were fewer than Shang's hundred."
translations.idiomatic: Yet government should prize simplicity: Xia's hundred offices were fewer than Shun's fifty, and Zhou's three hundred fewer than Shang's hundred."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「夏有亂政而作《禹刑》，商有亂政而作《湯刑》，周有亂政而作《九刑》。

translations.literal: He also said: "When Xia had disorderly government it produced the 'Punishments of Yu'; when Shang had disorderly government it produced the 'Punishments of Tang'; when Zhou had disorderly government it produced the 'Nine Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Disorder in Xia produced the Punishments of Yu; disorder in Shang produced the Punishments of Tang; disorder in Zhou produced the Nine Punishments.

sentences.zh: 衛鞅為秦制法，增鑿顛、抽脅、鑊烹等六篇，始皇為挾書律，此失於煩，不可不監。」

translations.literal: Wei Yang made law for Qin and added six chapters such as boring the crown, tearing out the ribs, and cauldron boiling; the First Emperor made the law against keeping books—here the fault lies in excess; it must not go unheeded."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yang codified Qin law and added six articles including boring the skull, tearing out the ribs, and cauldron boiling; the First Emperor added the law against private books—such excess must be watched against."

sentences.zh: 是時，太僕卿張道源建言：「官曹文簿繁總易欺，請減之以鈐吏奸。」

translations.literal: At that time the Minister of Studs Zhang Daoyuan proposed: "The documents of government offices are numerous and tangled, easy to deceive with—please reduce them to restrain clerical fraud."
translations.idiomatic: Then Minister of Studs Zhang Daoyuan proposed, "Government paperwork is so voluminous that clerks can easily cheat—please cut it back to curb their fraud."

sentences.zh: 公卿舉不為然，弈獨是之，為眾沮訾，不得行。

translations.literal: The high ministers generally disagreed; only Yi approved, was obstructed and reviled by the multitude, and the plan could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers mostly disagreed; Yi alone endorsed the idea, was blocked and denounced by the rest, and the proposal never took effect.

sentences.zh: 武德七年，上疏極詆浮圖法曰：

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wude he submitted a memorial vehemently denouncing the Buddhist law, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 7 he submitted a memorial fiercely attacking Buddhism, declaring:

sentences.zh: 西域之法，無君臣父子，以三塗六道嚇愚期庸。

translations.literal: The law of the Western Regions knows no ruler and subject, father and son; it frightens the foolish and coaxes the mediocre with the three paths and six destinies.
translations.idiomatic: The Western teaching knows neither ruler and subject nor father and son; it terrifies the simple and wheedles the mediocre with talk of three paths and six destinies.

sentences.zh: 追既往之罪，窺將來之福，至有身陷惡逆，獄中禮佛，口誦梵言，以圖偷免。

translations.literal: It pursues past sins and peeps at future blessings, until there are those sunk in grave treason who worship the Buddha in prison, recite Sanskrit phrases from their mouths, and seek to steal exemption.
translations.idiomatic: It dredges up past guilt and dangles future reward, so that men deep in capital crimes worship Buddha in jail, chant Sanskrit, and hope to cheat their way free.

sentences.zh: 且生死壽夭，本諸自然；

translations.literal: Moreover, life and death, longevity and early death, rest fundamentally in nature;
translations.idiomatic: Life, death, longevity, and early death belong to nature itself;

sentences.zh: 刑德威福，系之人主。

translations.literal: punishment and favor, authority and blessing, depend on the human ruler.
translations.idiomatic: while punishment, favor, authority, and blessing rest with the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 今其徒矯托，皆云由佛，攘天理，竊主權。

translations.literal: Now its followers falsely claim that all comes from the Buddha, usurping Heaven's principle and stealing the ruler's power.
translations.idiomatic: Its followers now falsely ascribe everything to Buddha, seizing Heaven's order and usurping the ruler's prerogatives.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「惟辟作福，惟辟作威，惟辟玉食。」

translations.literal: The Documents says: "Only the sovereign bestows blessing, only the sovereign exercises authority, only the sovereign enjoys fine food."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "Only the sovereign dispenses blessing, only the sovereign wields authority, only the sovereign enjoys fine fare.

sentences.zh: 臣有作福作威玉食，害於而家，凶于而國。

translations.literal: If subjects bestow blessing, exercise authority, and enjoy fine food, they harm their own house and bring ruin to their state.
translations.idiomatic: When subjects dispense blessing, wield authority, and enjoy fine fare, they harm their own house and bring disaster on the state."

sentences.zh: 五帝三王，未有佛法，君明臣忠，年祚長久。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors and Three Kings had no Buddhist law; rulers were enlightened and ministers loyal, and their reigns were long.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors and Three Kings knew no Buddhism; their rulers were wise, their ministers loyal, and their reigns long.

sentences.zh: 至漢明帝始立胡祠，然惟西域桑門自傳其教。

translations.literal: Only under Han Mingdi were barbarian shrines first established, yet only Western Region monks transmitted the teaching on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Not until Han Mingdi were foreign shrines founded, and even then only monks from the Western Regions spread the faith themselves.

sentences.zh: 西晉以上，不許中國髡發事胡。

translations.literal: Through Western Jin and earlier, Chinese were not permitted to shave their heads and serve the barbarian faith.
translations.idiomatic: Down through Western Jin, Chinese were forbidden to shave their heads and follow the foreign religion.

sentences.zh: 至石、苻亂華，乃弛厥禁，主庸臣佞，政虐祚短，事佛致然。

translations.literal: When the Shi and Fu clans threw China into chaos the ban was relaxed; rulers were mediocre, ministers fawning, government cruel and reigns brief—worship of Buddha brought this about.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shi and Fu regimes ravaged China the prohibition lapsed; mediocre rulers, fawning ministers, cruel rule, and short reigns all stemmed from devotion to Buddha.

sentences.zh: 梁武、齊襄尤足為戒。

translations.literal: Liang Wudi and Qi Xiangwang are especially fit to serve as warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang and Xiang of Qi are warnings enough.

sentences.zh: 昔褒姒一女，營惑幽王，能亡其國，況今僧尼十萬，刻繪泥像，以惑天下，有不亡乎？

translations.literal: Formerly Baosi, a single woman, beguiled King You and could destroy his state—how much more, when today monks and nuns number a hundred thousand, carving and painting clay images to bewitch the realm, can it fail to perish?
translations.idiomatic: Once Baosi alone beguiled King You and brought down his realm—how then, with a hundred thousand monks and nuns carving clay idols to delude the world, could the state not fall?

sentences.zh: 陛下以十萬之眾，自相夫婦，十年滋產，十年教訓，兵農兩足，利可勝既邪？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty took this multitude of a hundred thousand, paired them as husbands and wives, let them multiply for ten years and be taught for ten years, so that both armies and farmers were sufficient—could the profit surpass what is already lost?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty took those hundred thousand souls, paired them in marriage, let them breed and be trained for twenty years until arms and farms alike were full—could any gain outweigh what is already lost?

sentences.zh: 昔高齊章仇子他言僧尼塔廟，外見毀宰臣，內見疾妃嬙，陽讒陰謗，卒死都市，周武帝入齊，封寵其墓，臣竊賢之。

translations.literal: Formerly in Northern Qi, Zhangqiu Zita spoke against monks, nuns, pagodas, and temples; outwardly he seemed to slander chief ministers, inwardly he seemed to resent consorts and concubines; with open slander and covert defamation he died in the end in the market, yet when Zhou Wudi entered Qi he enfeoffed and favored his tomb—I privately admire him.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Qi, Zhangqiu Zita denounced monks, nuns, and their temples; he seemed to attack ministers abroad and resent the harem within, and open and covert slander alike brought him to execution in the capital—yet when Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi he honored Zita's tomb, and I for one admire him.

sentences.zh: 又上十二論，言益痛切。

translations.literal: He also submitted twelve treatises, their words still more bitter and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted twelve essays, their tone even sharper.

sentences.zh: 帝下弈議有司，唯道源佐其請。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Yi's proposal down to the relevant offices; only Daoyuan supported his request.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor referred Yi's proposal to the ministries; only Daoyuan backed it.

sentences.zh: 中書令蕭瑀曰：「佛，聖人也，非聖人者無法，請誅之。」

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Xiao Yu said: "The Buddha is a sage; those who are not sages have no law—please execute him."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Xiao Yu said, "Buddha is a sage; those who are not sages may not speak of law—execute this man."

sentences.zh: 弈曰：「禮，始事親，終事君。

translations.literal: Yi said: "In ritual, one begins by serving parents and ends by serving the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied, "Ritual begins with serving one's parents and ends with serving one's ruler.

sentences.zh: 而佛逃父出家，以匹夫抗天子，以繼體悖所親。

translations.literal: Yet the Buddha fled his father and left home, using a common man to resist the Son of Heaven and using the heir's body to betray those he should cherish.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Buddha fled his father and left home, setting a commoner against the Son of Heaven and making the heir betray his kin.

sentences.zh: 瑀非出空桑，乃尊其言，蓋所謂非孝者無親。」

translations.literal: Yu was not born from the hollow mulberry, yet he honors his words—this is what is called 'those without filial piety have no kin.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu was not born of the hollow mulberry tree, yet he reveres Buddha's words—the very thing meant by 'those without filial piety are without kin."

sentences.zh: 瑀不答，但合爪曰：「地獄正為是人設矣。」

translations.literal: Yu did not answer, but only pressed his palms and said: "Hell was indeed made for men like this."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said nothing, only pressed his palms together and said, "Hell was made for men like this."

sentences.zh: 帝善弈對，未及行，會傳位止。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved Yi's reply, but before it could be carried out, the abdication occurred and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved Yi's retort, but before action could be taken the abdication intervened and the matter ended.

sentences.zh: 初，九年，太白躔秦分，弈奏秦王當有天下，帝以奏付王。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the ninth year, Venus traversed the Qin asterism; Yi memorialized that the Prince of Qin ought to gain the realm, and the Emperor handed the memorial to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in year nine, Venus crossed the Qin sector; Yi reported that the Prince of Qin would gain the empire, and the Emperor passed the memorial to him.

sentences.zh: 及太宗即位，召賜食，謂曰：「向所奏，幾敗我！

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he summoned Yi, granted him food, and said: "What you memorialized before nearly ruined me!
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong succeeded, he summoned Yi, gave him a meal, and said, "That memorial of yours nearly destroyed me!

sentences.zh: 雖然，自今毋有所諱而不盡言。」

translations.literal: Nevertheless, from now on hold nothing back and speak fully."
translations.idiomatic: Even so, from now on speak your mind without reserve."

sentences.zh: 又嘗問：「卿拒佛法，奈何？」

translations.literal: He also once asked: "You reject the Buddhist law—how so?"
translations.idiomatic: He also once asked, "You reject Buddhism—why?"

sentences.zh: 弈曰：「佛，西胡黠人爾，欺訹夷狄以自神。

translations.literal: Yi said: "The Buddha is merely a crafty man of the Western barbarians, deceiving and deluding the Yi and Di to make himself divine.
translations.idiomatic: Yi answered, "Buddha is only a cunning barbarian of the west, tricking the frontier peoples into thinking him divine.

sentences.zh: 至入中國，而鏚兒幻夫摸象莊、老以文飾之，有害國家，而無補百姓也。」

translations.literal: When he entered China, low conjurers and illusionists, like men groping the elephant, draped him in the literary adornments of Zhuangzi and Laozi—harmful to the state and of no benefit to the common people."
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached China, street conjurers and illusionists dressed him up in Zhuangzi and Laozi—harmful to the state and useless to the people."

sentences.zh: 帝異之。

translations.literal: The Emperor marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was struck by his words.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十三年，卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhenguan he died, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhenguan 13, at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 弈病，未嘗問醫，忽酣臥，蹶然悟曰：「吾死矣乎！」

translations.literal: When Yi fell ill he never consulted physicians; suddenly he slept deeply in drunkenness, started awake, and said: "Am I dying?"
translations.idiomatic: When ill he never called a doctor; once, after heavy drinking, he woke with a start and cried, "Am I dying?"

sentences.zh: 即自志曰：「傅弈，青山白雲人也。

translations.literal: He at once wrote his own epitaph: "Fu Yi, a man of green mountains and white clouds.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote his own epitaph at once: "Fu Yi—a man of green hills and white clouds.

sentences.zh: 以醉死，嗚乎！」

translations.literal: Died drunk—alas!"
translations.idiomatic: Died drunk—alas!"

sentences.zh: 遺言戒子：「《六經》名教言，若可習也；

translations.literal: His testament admonished his sons: "The teachings of the Six Classics in the orthodox tradition—if they can be studied;
translations.idiomatic: He charged his sons, "Study the moral teachings of the Six Classics if you will;

sentences.zh: 妖胡之法，慎勿為。

translations.literal: the law of the demonic barbarians—be careful never to practice it.
translations.idiomatic: but never follow the barbarian cult.

sentences.zh: 吾死當倮葬。」

translations.literal: When I die, bury me unclothed."
translations.idiomatic: Bury me naked when I die."

sentences.zh: 弈雖善數，然嘗自言其學不可以傳。

translations.literal: Although Yi was skilled in numerology, he once said himself that his learning could not be transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Though skilled in numerology, he said his art could not be passed on.

sentences.zh: 又注《老子》，並集晉、魏以來與佛議駁者為《高識篇》。

translations.literal: He also annotated the Laozi and collected refutations of Buddhism from Jin and Wei onward into the "Treatise on Lofty Insight."
translations.idiomatic: He also annotated the Laozi and compiled anti-Buddhist writings from Jin and Wei onward into the Treatise on Lofty Insight.

sentences.zh: 武德時，所改漏刻，定十二軍號，皆詔弈雲。

translations.literal: In the Wude era, the revised clepsydra graduations and the fixing of the twelve army designations were all ordered on Yi's advice.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude, revisions to the water clock and the twelve army titles all followed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 呂才呂才，博州清平人。

translations.literal: Lu Cai, Lu Cai, was a native of Qingping in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Cai was from Qingping in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀時，祖孝孫增損樂律，與音家王長通、白明達更質難，不能決。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, Zu Xiaosun revised the musical pitches; he and the music masters Wang Changtong and Bai Mingda repeatedly questioned and challenged one another but could not settle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan, Zu Xiaosun revised the pitch standard; he and the masters Wang Changtong and Bai Mingda debated back and forth without resolution.

sentences.zh: 太宗詔侍臣舉善音者，中書令溫彥博白才天悟絕人，聞見一接，輒窮其妙；

translations.literal: Taizong ordered the attendant ministers to recommend those skilled in music; Chief Councilor Wen Yanbo reported that Cai's heaven-given insight was beyond other men—on a single hearing or sight he would exhaust its subtlety;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong asked his ministers to name men skilled in music; Chief Councilor Wen Yanbo said Cai's gift was matchless and that one exposure to any problem exhausted its secrets;

sentences.zh: 侍中王珪、魏征盛稱才制尺八凡十二枚，長短不同，與律諧契。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-chief Wang Gui and Wei Zheng greatly praised the twelve chi-eight pipes Cai had made, each of different length, all in harmony with the pitch standard.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui and Wei Zheng praised the twelve chi-eight pipes he had made, each of a different length yet all in accord with the pitch standard.

sentences.zh: 即召才直弘文館，參論樂事。

translations.literal: Cai was immediately summoned to serve directly in the Hongwen Academy to take part in discussions on music.
translations.idiomatic: Cai was summoned straight to the Hongwen Academy to join the deliberations on music.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗覽周武帝《三局象經》，不能通，或言太子洗馬蔡允恭能之，召問允恭，少通其略，老乃忘。

translations.literal: The Emperor once perused Emperor Wu of Zhou's Classic of Three-Board Chess and could not understand it; someone said the Crown Prince's Study Aide Cai Yungong could do so. He was summoned and questioned; in youth he had grasped its outline, but in old age he forgot.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once read Emperor Wu of Zhou's Classic of Three-Board Chess and could not follow it; someone said Cai Yungong, Study Aide to the Heir Apparent, understood it. Yungong had known its outline in youth but forgot it in age.

sentences.zh: 試問才，退一昔即解，具圖以聞。

translations.literal: Cai was tested; after one evening's withdrawal he understood it, drew the full diagrams, and reported them.
translations.idiomatic: Cai was tested; after a single night he mastered it, drew the full diagrams, and submitted them.

sentences.zh: 允恭記其舊，與才正同，由是知名。

translations.literal: Yungong recalled his former knowledge, which matched Cai's exactly, and from this Cai became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong's old recollection matched Cai's solution exactly, and from that Cai became famous.

sentences.zh: 擢累太常博士。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 帝病陰陽家所傳書多謬偽淺惡，世益拘畏，命才與宿學老師刪落煩訛，掇可用者為五十三篇，合舊書四十七，凡百篇，詔頒天下。

translations.literal: The Emperor was troubled that the books transmitted by the yin-yang masters were mostly false, shallow, and vile, and that the age grew ever more constrained and fearful; he ordered Cai and veteran scholars to delete redundancies and errors, gather what could be used into fifty-three chapters, join them with forty-seven old books, one hundred chapters in all, and promulgate them throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor disliked the yin-yang masters' books as mostly false, shallow, and crude, and that the world grew ever more fearful of omens; he had Cai and senior scholars cut redundancies and errors, select fifty-three usable chapters, combine them with forty-seven older texts for one hundred chapters in all, and promulgate them empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 才於持議儒而不俚，以經誼推處其驗術，諸家共訶短之，又舉世相惑以禍福，終莫悟雲。

translations.literal: In his arguments Cai was scholarly without being vulgar, using canonical principles to weigh his prognostic techniques, yet all schools together reviled and faulted him; moreover the whole world was mutually deluded by fortune and calamity, and in the end none understood.
translations.idiomatic: Cai argued in a scholarly, not vulgar, way, weighing divinatory arts by canonical principle, yet every school faulted him; the world remained enthralled by fortune and disaster, and no one ever learned better.

sentences.zh: 才之言不甚文，要欲救俗失，切時事，俾易曉也。

translations.literal: Cai's words were not very literary; essentially he wished to remedy popular errors, cut close to current affairs, and make them easy to understand.
translations.idiomatic: Cai's prose was plain; he meant to correct popular error, speak to present concerns, and be easily understood.

sentences.zh: 故叕刂其三篇。

translations.literal: Therefore three of his chapters are abridged here.
translations.idiomatic: Three of his chapters are therefore excerpted below.

sentences.zh: 《卜宅篇》曰：

translations.literal: The "Chapter on Dwelling Selection" says:
translations.idiomatic: The Chapter on Dwelling Selection reads:

sentences.zh: 《易》稱「上古穴居而野處，後世聖人易之以宮室。

translations.literal: The Changes says: "In high antiquity men dwelt in caves and lived in the wild; later sages replaced this with palaces and chambers.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "In high antiquity men lived in caves and dwelt in the wild; later sages replaced that with houses and halls.

sentences.zh: 蓋取諸《大壯》」。

translations.literal: This was taken from the hexagram Powerful."
translations.idiomatic: That change was drawn from the hexagram Powerful."

sentences.zh: 殷、周時有卜擇之文，《詩》稱「相其陰陽」，《書》卜洛食。

translations.literal: In Yin and Zhou there were texts on divination and selection; the Odes says "observe its yin and yang," and the Documents records divining Luo and the offering.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Zhou already had texts on site selection; the Odes speak of observing yin and yang, and the Documents record divining at Luo.

sentences.zh: 近世乃有五姓，謂宮也，商也，角也，徵也，羽也，以為天下萬物悉配屬之，以處吉凶，然言皆不類。

translations.literal: In recent times there came the Five Surnames, called palace, merchant, horn, chime, and feather, holding that all things under heaven could be assigned to them to determine fortune and calamity—yet the doctrine does not cohere.
translations.idiomatic: Lately there is the doctrine of Five Surnames—palace, merchant, horn, chime, and feather—by which all things are assigned to fix fortune and disaster, yet the theory never holds together.

sentences.zh: 如張、王為商，武、庾為羽，是以音相諧附；

translations.literal: For example Zhang and Wang are merchant, Wu and Yu are feather—here they are matched by sound;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang and Wang count as merchant, Wu and Yu as feather, because the names echo the pitch names;

sentences.zh: 至柳為宮，趙為角，則又不然。

translations.literal: but when Liu is palace and Zhao is horn, it no longer works.
translations.idiomatic: yet Liu as palace and Zhao as horn plainly fail.

sentences.zh: 其間一姓而兩屬，復姓數字不得所歸。

translations.literal: Among them one surname may belong to two categories, and compound surnames of several characters have nowhere to be assigned.
translations.idiomatic: Some surnames fall under two categories at once, and compound surnames of several characters fit nowhere.

sentences.zh: 是直野人巫師說爾。

translations.literal: This is simply the talk of rustic shamans.
translations.idiomatic: That is nothing but village sorcery.

sentences.zh: 按《堪輿經》，黃帝對天老，始言五姓。

translations.literal: According to the Classic of Sitings, when Huangdi addressed Tianlao, the Five Surnames were first mentioned.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Sitings records Huangdi addressing Tianlao as the first mention of the Five Surnames.

sentences.zh: 且黃帝時獨姬、薑數姓耳，後世賜族者浸多，然管、蔡、郕、霍、魯、衛、毛、聃、郜、雍、曹、滕、畢、原、酆、郇本之姬姓，孔、殷、宋、華、向、蕭、亳、皇甫本之子姓，至因官命氏，因邑賜族，本同末異，叵為配宮商哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, in Huangdi's time there were only the Ji and Jiang surnames; later enfeoffed clans grew ever more numerous—yet Guan, Cai, Cheng, Huo, Lu, Wei, Mao, Dan, Gao, Yong, Cao, Teng, Bi, Yuan, Feng, and Xun derive from the Ji surname; Kong, Yin, Song, Hua, Xiang, Xiao, Bo, and Huangfu derive from the Zi surname; then there are surnames taken from offices and surnames granted from towns—same in origin, different in outcome—how can they be assigned to palace and merchant?
translations.idiomatic: In Huangdi's day only the Ji and Jiang lines existed; later enfeoffed houses multiplied—Guan, Cai, Lu, Wei, and the rest stem from Ji; Kong, Song, Yin, and the rest from Zi; still others take names from offices or fiefs—same roots, divergent branches—how could they be sorted into palace and merchant tones?

sentences.zh: 春秋以陳、衛、秦為水姓，齊、鄭、宋為火姓，或所出之祖，所分之星，所居之地，以著由來，非宮、商、角、徵、羽相管攝也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals treats Chen, Wei, and Qin as water surnames and Qi, Zheng, and Song as fire surnames—perhaps by the ancestor from whom they sprang, the star they were allotted, or the land they dwelt in, to show their origin—not by palace, merchant, horn, chime, and feather governing one another.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals call Chen, Wei, and Qin water clans and Qi, Zheng, and Song fire clans—marking ancestry, allotted stars, or dwelling places, not the five musical notes as rulers of fate.

sentences.zh: 《祿命篇》曰：

translations.literal: The "Chapter on Fortune and Fate" says:
translations.idiomatic: The Chapter on Fortune and Fate reads:

sentences.zh: 漢宋忠、賈誼譏司馬季主曰：「卜筮者高人祿命，以悅人心；

translations.literal: In Han, Song Zhong and Jia Yi mocked Sima Jizhu, saying: "Diviners exalt fortune and fate to please men's hearts;
translations.idiomatic: In Han, Song Zhong and Jia Yi mocked Sima Jizhu: "Diviners inflate fortune and fate to please their clients;

sentences.zh: 矯言禍福，以規人財。」

translations.literal: they twist words of fortune and calamity to scheme for others' wealth."
translations.idiomatic: they twist omens of fortune and disaster to extort money.

sentences.zh: 王充曰：「見骨體，知命祿；

translations.literal: Wang Chong said: "Seeing the bone structure, one knows fortune and fate;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chong said, "See the bones and you know fortune and fate;

sentences.zh: 見命祿，知骨體。」

translations.literal: seeing fortune and fate, one knows the bone structure."
translations.idiomatic: see fortune and fate and you know the bones.

sentences.zh: 此則言祿命尚矣。

translations.literal: Thus the doctrine of fortune and fate has long been honored.
translations.idiomatic: So the cult of fortune and fate is ancient indeed.

sentences.zh: 推索本原，固不其然。

translations.literal: Tracing it to its root, it is fundamentally not so.
translations.idiomatic: Traced to its root, it simply is not true.

sentences.zh: 「積善之家，必有餘慶」，豈建祿而後吉乎？

translations.literal: "The house that accumulates goodness will surely have surplus blessing"—must blessing come only after establishing fortune?
translations.idiomatic: "The house that accumulates goodness will have surplus blessing"—must blessing wait on a chart of official fortune?

sentences.zh: 「積惡之家，必有餘殃」，豈劫殺而後災乎？

translations.literal: "The house that accumulates evil will surely have surplus calamity"—must disaster come only after robbery and slaughter?
translations.idiomatic: "The house that accumulates evil will have surplus disaster"—must disaster wait on violent robbery in the chart?

sentences.zh: 「皇天無親，常與善人」，天人之交如影響。

translations.literal: "August Heaven is without partiality and constantly aids the good"—the interaction of Heaven and man is like shadow and echo.
translations.idiomatic: "August Heaven is impartial and ever aids the good"—Heaven and man answer each other like shadow and echo.

sentences.zh: 「有夏多罪，天命剿絕」；

translations.literal: "The Xia had many crimes, and Heaven's mandate cut them off";
translations.idiomatic: "The Xia were steeped in crime, and Heaven's mandate destroyed them";

sentences.zh: 宋景脩德，妖星退舍。

translations.literal: Duke Jing of Song cultivated virtue, and the malign star withdrew from its lodge.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Jing of Song cultivated virtue, the baleful star retreated from its station.

sentences.zh: 「學也祿在某中」，不生當建學。

translations.literal: "Learning too has Salary in a certain position"—if one is not born at Establishment, one ought to pursue learning.
translations.idiomatic: "Scholarly office too depends on Salary falling in a given palace"—unless born at Establishment, one must take the scholar's path.

sentences.zh: 文王憂勤損壽，非初值空亡；

translations.literal: King Wen's worry and diligence shortened his years—it was not because his chart first met Empty Void.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen's anxious toil shortened his life; that was not because his nativity first struck Empty Void.

sentences.zh: 長平坑降卒，非俱犯三刑；

translations.literal: The burying alive of surrendered troops at Changping was not because all of them had violated the Three Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The slaughter of surrendered troops at Changping did not happen because every man there had violated the Three Punishments.

sentences.zh: 南陽多近親，非俱當六合；

translations.literal: Nanyang has many close-kin marriages—it is not because all were fated for the Six Harmonies.
translations.idiomatic: Close-kin marriages are common in Nanyang—not because every household was destined for the Six Harmonies.

sentences.zh: 曆陽成湖，不共河魁；

translations.literal: Liyang became a lake—they did not all share the River Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Liyang sank into a lake, the victims did not all share the same River Chief star.

sentences.zh: 蜀郡炎火，不盡災厄。

translations.literal: The conflagration in Shu Commandery did not bring disaster to every soul.
translations.idiomatic: The great fire in Shu Commandery did not afflict everyone with calamity.

sentences.zh: 世有同建與祿，而貴賤殊域；

translations.literal: In the world there are men with the same Establishment and Salary, yet noble and base stand worlds apart.
translations.idiomatic: Men born with the same Establishment and Salary can yet stand at opposite extremes of rank and fortune.

sentences.zh: 共命若胎，而夭壽異科。

translations.literal: They share a nativity as twins might, yet short life and long life fall in different categories.
translations.idiomatic: They may share a birth chart as twins do, yet one dies young while another lives out his years.

sentences.zh: 魯桓公六年七月，子同生，是為莊公。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Duke Huan of Lu, in the seventh month, Zitong was born; this was Duke Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Duke Huan of Lu, Zitong was born—the future Duke Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 按曆，歲在乙亥，月建申，然則值祿空亡，據法應窮賤。

translations.literal: By the calendar, the year stood in yihai and the month was established in shen; thus Salary fell in Empty Void, and by the method he should have been poor and base.
translations.idiomatic: By the calendar the year was yihai and the month established in shen, placing Salary in Empty Void; by the rules he ought to have ended poor and lowly.

sentences.zh: 又觸句絞六害，偝驛馬，身克驛馬三刑，法無官。

translations.literal: He also struck Knot Strangulation and the Six Harms, Opposed Salary and the Post Horse, and his body overcame the Post Horse in the Three Punishments; by the method he should have had no office.
translations.idiomatic: His chart also hit Knot Strangulation and the Six Harms, Opposed Salary and the Post Horse, with the body conquering the Post Horse under the Three Punishments—by the rules he should never have held office.

sentences.zh: 命火也，生當病鄉，法曰「為人尪弱矬陋」，而《詩》言莊公曰：「猗嗟昌兮，頎而長兮。

translations.literal: His fate was Fire, and he was born in the Sickness Sector; the method says, "The man will be frail, weak, short, and ugly," yet the Odes speak of Duke Zhuang, saying, "Ah, how splendid he is, tall and long he is.
translations.idiomatic: His natal element was Fire and his birth fell in the Sickness Sector; the method declares, "Such a man will be frail, puny, short, and ugly," yet the Odes praise Duke Zhuang: "How splendid he is—tall and stately.

sentences.zh: 美目揚兮，巧趨蹌兮。」

translations.literal: Bright are his eyes and lifted his glance; skillful is his gait and nimble his step."
translations.idiomatic: Bright his eyes, lifted his gaze; graceful his stride, nimble his step.

sentences.zh: 唯向命一物，法當壽，而公薨止四十五。

translations.literal: Only one point in the chart pointed to long life, yet the duke died at only forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Only one feature of the chart promised long life, yet the duke died at forty-five.

sentences.zh: 一不驗。

translations.literal: The first case fails verification.
translations.idiomatic: The first prediction does not hold.

sentences.zh: 秦昭襄王四十八年，始皇帝生以正月，故名政。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year of King Zhaoxiang of Qin, the First Emperor was born in the first month, and therefore was named Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year of King Zhaoxiang of Qin, the future First Emperor was born in the first month and was therefore named Zheng.

sentences.zh: 是歲壬寅正月，命偝祿，於法無官，假得祿，奴婢應少。

translations.literal: That year was renyin in the first month; his fate had Opposed Salary, and by the method he should have had no office; even had he possessed Salary, his servants and maids should have been few.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the renyin year his chart showed Opposed Salary; by the rules he should have held no office, and even with Salary he should have kept few servants.

sentences.zh: 又破驛馬三刑，身克驛馬，法望官不到。

translations.literal: He also broke the Post Horse in the Three Punishments, and his body overcame the Post Horse; by the method the office he hoped for would never come.
translations.idiomatic: His chart also broke the Post Horse under the Three Punishments, with the body conquering the Post Horse—by the rules the high office he might have sought would never arrive.

sentences.zh: 命金也，正月為絕，無始有終，老而吉。

translations.literal: His fate was Metal; the first month was Cutoff—no beginning yet an end—and old age was auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: His natal element was Metal; the first month marked Cutoff—"no beginning, yet an end"—and old age was said to be fortunate.

sentences.zh: 又建命生，法當壽，帝崩時不過五十。

translations.literal: He was also born under Establishment Fate, and by the method he should have been long-lived, yet when the emperor died he was not yet fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He was also born under Establishment Fate, which by the rules promised long life, yet he died before he reached fifty.

sentences.zh: 二不驗。

translations.literal: The second case fails verification.
translations.idiomatic: The second prediction does not hold.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝以乙酉歲七月七日平旦生，當祿空亡，於法無官。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han was born on the seventh day of the seventh month of the yiyou year, at dawn; Salary fell in Empty Void, and by the method he should have had no office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han was born at dawn on the seventh day of the seventh month in the yiyou year; with Salary in Empty Void, the rules denied him office.

sentences.zh: 雖向驛馬，乃隔四辰，法少無官，老而吉；

translations.literal: Although he faced the Post Horse, it was separated by four branches; by the method he should have had no office in youth and only prospered in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Though his chart faced the Post Horse, four branches stood between them; by the rules he should have held no office in youth and only fared well in old age.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，年十六，末年戶口減耗。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu took the throne at sixteen, and in his later years the population dwindled.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu ascended the throne at sixteen, yet in his later years the realm's population shrank.

sentences.zh: 三不驗。

translations.literal: The third case fails verification.
translations.idiomatic: The third prediction does not hold.

sentences.zh: 後魏高祖孝文皇帝生皇興元年八月，是歲丁未，為偝祿命與驛馬三刑，身克驛馬，於法無官。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen, the High Ancestor of Later Wei, was born in the eighth month of the first year of Huangxing; that year was dingwei, and his fate showed Opposed Salary with the Post Horse in the Three Punishments; his body overcame the Post Horse, and by the method he should have had no office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen, High Ancestor of Northern Wei, was born in the eighth month of Huangxing 1, a dingwei year; his chart showed Opposed Salary with the Post Horse in the Three Punishments and the body conquering the Post Horse—by the rules he should never have held office.

sentences.zh: 又生父死中，法不見父，而孝文受其父顯祖之禪。

translations.literal: He was also born in the Father-Death phase, and by the method he should not have seen his father, yet Xiaowen received the abdication from his father, Emperor Xianzu.
translations.idiomatic: He was also born in the Father-Death phase, which by the rules meant he should never have seen his father, yet Xiaowen received the abdication from his father, Emperor Xianzu.

sentences.zh: 禮，君未逾年，不得正位，故天子無父，事三老也。

translations.literal: By rite, if a ruler has not passed a full year of mourning, he may not take the formal seat; hence the Son of Heaven has no father and serves the Three Elders instead.
translations.idiomatic: Rites hold that a ruler who has not completed a full year of mourning may not take formal possession of the throne; thus the Son of Heaven has no living father and instead honors the Three Elders.

sentences.zh: 孝文率天下生子墓中，法宜嫡子，雖有次子，當早卒，而高祖長子先被弑，次子義隆享國。

translations.literal: Among all sons born under heaven in the Tomb phase, the method says there should be a legitimate heir; though there be a second son, he should die early—yet the High Ancestor's eldest son was first assassinated, and the second son, Yilong, came to hold the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Of sons born across the realm in the Tomb phase, the method promises a legitimate heir; though a second son exists, he should die young—yet Xiaowen's eldest son was murdered first, and the second, Yilong, inherited the throne.

sentences.zh: 又生祖祿下，法得嫡孫財若祿；

translations.literal: He was also born beneath Ancestral Salary, and by the method a legitimate grandson should receive wealth like Salary.
translations.idiomatic: He was also born beneath Ancestral Salary, which by the rules should have brought a legitimate grandson wealth equal to Salary itself.

sentences.zh: 其孫劭、浚皆篡逆，幾失宗祧。

translations.literal: Yet his grandsons Shao and Jun both rose in rebellion and nearly lost the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his grandsons Shao and Jun both rebelled and nearly destroyed the imperial line.

sentences.zh: 五不驗。

translations.literal: The fifth case fails verification.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth prediction does not hold.

sentences.zh: 《葬篇》曰：

translations.literal: The "Chapter on Burial" says:
translations.idiomatic: The Chapter on Burial reads:

sentences.zh: 《易》稱：「古之葬者，衣之以薪，不封不樹，喪期無數，後世聖人易之以棺槨。

translations.literal: The Changes say: "The ancients in burying the dead clothed them in firewood, raised no mound and planted no tree; mourning had no fixed term, until later sages replaced this with coffin and outer coffin.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "The ancients buried the dead wrapped in firewood, neither heaping earth nor planting trees; mourning had no fixed duration, until later sages replaced this with inner and outer coffins.

sentences.zh: 蓋取諸《大過》。」

translations.literal: This was taken from Great Excess."
translations.idiomatic: That practice was drawn from the hexagram Great Excess.

sentences.zh: 《經》曰：「葬者，藏也，欲人之弗得見也。」

translations.literal: The Classic says: "To bury is to hide, so that men may not see."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic says: "Burial means concealment, so that the dead may not be seen.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「卜其宅兆，而安厝之。」

translations.literal: It also says: "Divine the dwelling and its omens, and lay the body to rest in peace."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Divine the grave site and its signs, and inter the body in peace.

sentences.zh: 以是為感慕之所也，魂神之宅也。

translations.literal: By this it becomes a place for yearning and remembrance, a dwelling for soul and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the tomb becomes a place of longing and remembrance—the home of soul and spirit.

sentences.zh: 朝市貿遷不可知，石泉頹齧不可常，是其謀及卜筮，庶無後艱，斯則備於慎終之禮也。

translations.literal: Markets and capitals shift in ways none can foresee; stone and spring erode and crumble without lasting—therefore planning extends to divination and milfoil, so that later hardship may be avoided; this is what the rites of careful ending provide for.
translations.idiomatic: Markets and capitals shift unpredictably; stone cliffs and springs erode and cannot endure—hence the ancients turned to divination and milfoil, hoping to spare posterity later hardship. That is what the rites of reverent closure were meant to secure.

sentences.zh: 後代葬說出於巫史，一物有失，便謂災及死生，多為妨禁，以售其術，附妄憑妖，至其書乃有百二十家。

translations.literal: Later generations' theories of burial came from shamans and clerks; if one thing was amiss, they would say disaster touched life and death, imposing many taboos to sell their arts, attaching falsehoods to spirits and omens, until their books numbered one hundred and twenty schools.
translations.idiomatic: Later burial lore came from shamans and record-keepers; one misstep, they claimed, would bring disaster upon the living and the dead. They piled up taboos to sell their craft, draping nonsense in spirits and portents, until such books numbered a hundred and twenty schools.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》：「王者七日而殯，七月而葬；

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals say: "A king lies in state seven days and is buried in the seventh month;
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals say: "A king lies in state for seven days and is buried in the seventh month;

sentences.zh: 諸侯五日而殯，五月而葬；

translations.literal: a feudal lord lies in state five days and is buried in the fifth month;
translations.idiomatic: a feudal lord lies in state for five days and is buried in the fifth month;

sentences.zh: 大夫三月，士庶人逾月而已。」

translations.literal: a grandee three months, and officers and commoners after a month, no more."
translations.idiomatic: a grandee for three months, and officers and commoners after a month—no longer.

sentences.zh: 貴賤不同，禮亦異數。

translations.literal: Noble and base differ, and the rites differ in number.
translations.idiomatic: Rank differs, and so do the prescribed intervals.

sentences.zh: 此直為赴吊遠近之期，量事制法。

translations.literal: This was simply to set the term for mourners near and far, measuring affairs and establishing law.
translations.idiomatic: These intervals simply fixed the time for mourners near and far to assemble—rules scaled to circumstance.

sentences.zh: 故先期而葬，謂之不懷也；

translations.literal: Hence to bury before the term is called lack of affection;
translations.idiomatic: To bury before the appointed term is called being unfeeling;

sentences.zh: 後期不葬，謂之殆禮也。

translations.literal: to fail to bury after the term is called neglect of rite.
translations.idiomatic: to leave the dead unburied after the term is called neglect of rite.

sentences.zh: 此則葬有定期，不擇年與月，一也。

translations.literal: Thus burial has a fixed term and does not select year or month—this is the first point.
translations.idiomatic: Burial therefore has a fixed interval and does not depend on choosing year or month—that is the first point.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「丁巳，葬定公，雨，不克葬，至於戊午襄事。」

translations.literal: It also says: "On ding-si, Duke Ding was buried; rain fell and the burial could not be completed, until on wu-wu the rites were finished."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "On ding-si they began burying Duke Ding, but rain prevented the burial; not until wu-wu were the rites completed.

sentences.zh: 君子善之。

translations.literal: The gentleman approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman praised this.

sentences.zh: 《禮》「卜先遠日」者，自末而進，避不懷也。

translations.literal: The Rites' "divine the more distant day first" means to proceed from the latest date backward, avoiding lack of affection.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rites speak of "divining the more distant day first," they mean working backward from the latest permissible date to avoid being unfeeling.

sentences.zh: 今法己亥日用葬最凶，春秋是日葬者二十餘族。

translations.literal: In the current method, ji-hai is the most inauspicious day for burial, yet in the Spring and Autumn more than twenty clans were buried on that day.
translations.idiomatic: Current methods call ji-hai the most ill-omened day for burial, yet the Spring and Autumn record more than twenty clans buried on that very day.

sentences.zh: 此葬不擇日，二也。

translations.literal: This shows that burial does not select the day—the second point.
translations.idiomatic: Burial, then, does not depend on choosing the day—that is the second point.

sentences.zh: 《禮》：「周尚赤，大事用旦；

translations.literal: The Rites say: "Zhou honored red, and great affairs were performed at dawn;
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say: "Zhou honored red and performed great affairs at dawn;

sentences.zh: 殷尚白，大事用日中；

translations.literal: Yin honored white, and great affairs were performed at midday;
translations.idiomatic: Yin honored white and performed great affairs at midday;

sentences.zh: 夏尚黑，大事用昏。」

translations.literal: Xia honored black, and great affairs were performed at dusk."
translations.idiomatic: Xia honored black and performed great affairs at dusk.

sentences.zh: 大事者何？

translations.literal: What are great affairs?
translations.idiomatic: What are "great affairs"?

sentences.zh: 喪禮也。

translations.literal: Funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 此直取當代所尚，而不擇時早晚也。

translations.literal: This simply followed what the age honored and did not select whether the hour was early or late.
translations.idiomatic: Each dynasty simply followed what it honored and did not fuss over whether the hour was early or late.

sentences.zh: 鄭卿子產及子太叔葬簡公。

translations.literal: Minister Zichan of Zheng and Z Taishu buried Duke Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Zichan of Zheng and Z Taishu buried Duke Jian.

sentences.zh: 於是，司墓大夫室當柩路，若壞其室，即平旦而堋；

translations.literal: At that time the tomb-keeper grandee's house stood in the path of the bier; if they destroyed the house, they would lower the coffin at dawn;
translations.idiomatic: The tomb-keeper's house then blocked the bier's route; if they tore it down, the coffin would be lowered at dawn;

sentences.zh: 不壞其室，即日中而堋。

translations.literal: if they did not destroy the house, they would lower the coffin at midday.
translations.idiomatic: if they left the house standing, the coffin would be lowered at midday.

sentences.zh: 子產不欲壞室，欲待日中。

translations.literal: Zichan did not wish to destroy the house and wanted to wait until midday.
translations.idiomatic: Zichan refused to destroy the house and wished to wait until midday.

sentences.zh: 子太叔曰：「若日中而堋，恐久勞諸侯大夫來會葬者。」

translations.literal: Z Taishu said: "If we lower the coffin at midday, I fear we will long weary the feudal lords and grandees who have come to the funeral."
translations.idiomatic: Z Taishu said, "If we wait until midday to lower the coffin, I fear we will keep the feudal lords and grandees who have come to mourn waiting too long.

sentences.zh: 然子產、太叔不問時之得失，惟論人事可否而已。

translations.literal: Yet Zichan and Taishu did not ask whether the hour was auspicious or ill-omened; they discussed only whether the human affair could be done.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zichan and Taishu never asked whether the hour was lucky or unlucky; they debated only whether the human task could be carried out.

sentences.zh: 曾子曰：「葬逢日蝕，舍于路左，待明而行。」

translations.literal: Zengzi said: "If burial meets a solar eclipse, lodge by the left of the road and wait for dawn before proceeding."
translations.idiomatic: Zengzi said, "If a burial coincides with a solar eclipse, halt by the left side of the road and wait for dawn before going on.

sentences.zh: 所以備非常也。

translations.literal: This was to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: That was to prepare for the unforeseen.

sentences.zh: 按法，葬家多取乾、艮二時，乃近夜半，文與禮乖。

translations.literal: By the current method, burial masters mostly take the Qian and Gen hours, which are near midnight—words and rites are at odds.
translations.idiomatic: By current methods, burial masters mostly choose the Qian and Gen hours, near midnight—plainly at odds with the rites.

sentences.zh: 此葬不擇時，三也。

translations.literal: This shows that burial does not select the hour—the third point.
translations.idiomatic: Burial, then, does not depend on choosing the hour—that is the third point.

sentences.zh: 《經》曰：「立身行道，揚名於後世，以顯父母。」

translations.literal: The Classic says: "Establish yourself and walk in the Way; spread your name through later ages and thereby honor your parents."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic says: "Establish yourself and walk in the Way; win a name that shines through later ages and thereby honor your parents.

sentences.zh: 《易》謂：「聖人之大寶曰位，何以守位曰仁。」

translations.literal: The Changes say: "The great treasure of the sage is rank; by what does he keep rank? By benevolence."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "The sage's great treasure is rank; by what does he keep rank? By benevolence.

sentences.zh: 而法曰：「官爵富貴，葬可致也；

translations.literal: Yet the method says: "Office, title, wealth, and honor can be brought by burial;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the geomancers say: "Office, rank, wealth, and honor can be secured through burial;

sentences.zh: 年壽修促，子姓蕃衍，葬可招也。」

translations.literal: length or shortness of life, and the flourishing of sons and clans, can be summoned by burial."
translations.idiomatic: long or short life and the flourishing of one's line can be summoned through burial.

sentences.zh: 夫日慎一日，澤及無疆；

translations.literal: If one is careful day by day, blessing reaches without limit;
translations.idiomatic: If one is careful day by day, blessing extends without bound;

sentences.zh: 德則不建，而祚乃無永。

translations.literal: if virtue is not built up, then fortune cannot long endure.
translations.idiomatic: if virtue is never cultivated, fortune cannot long endure.

sentences.zh: 臧孫有後於魯，不聞葬得吉也；

translations.literal: Zangsun left descendants in Lu—I have never heard that this came from an auspicious burial;
translations.idiomatic: Zangsun left descendants in Lu—no one says that came from a lucky tomb;

sentences.zh: 若敖絕祀于荊，不聞葬得凶也。

translations.literal: Ruo'ao's sacrifice was cut off in Chu—I have never heard that this came from an inauspicious burial.
translations.idiomatic: the Ruo'ao line died out in Chu—no one says that came from an unlucky tomb.

sentences.zh: 此葬有吉凶不可信，四也。

translations.literal: Thus the auspicious and inauspicious in burial cannot be trusted—the fourth point.
translations.idiomatic: The claim that burial brings good or ill fortune cannot be trusted—that is the fourth point.

sentences.zh: 今法皆據五姓為之。

translations.literal: The current method is entirely based on the Five Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Current methods are built entirely on the Five Surnames.

sentences.zh: 古之葬，並在國都之北，趙氏之葬，在九原，漢家山陵，或散處諸域，又何上利下利、大墓小墓為哉？

translations.literal: Burials of old were all north of the capital; the Zhao clan was buried at Jiuyuan, and the Han imperial tombs were scattered across many regions—what then of upper benefit, lower benefit, great tomb, and small tomb?
translations.idiomatic: Ancient burials lay north of the capital; the Zhao were buried at Jiuyuan, while Han imperial tombs were scattered across the realm—what then of "upper benefit," "lower benefit," great tombs, and small tombs?

sentences.zh: 然劉之子孫，本支不絕，趙後與六國等王。

translations.literal: Yet the Liu descendants never ceased in the main line, and the Zhao later stood equal with the kings of the Six States.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Liu line never died out in its main branch, and the Zhao later ranked as equals among the kings of the Six States.

sentences.zh: 此則葬用五姓不可信，五也。

translations.literal: Thus burial by the Five Surnames cannot be trusted—the fifth point.
translations.idiomatic: Burial by the Five Surnames, then, cannot be trusted—that is the fifth point.

sentences.zh: 且人有初賤而後貴、始泰而終否者。

translations.literal: Moreover, there are men first base and later noble, first prosperous and later ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, some men begin in low estate and rise to honor, or start in prosperity and end in ruin.

sentences.zh: 子文為令尹，三仕三已，展禽三黜于士師。

translations.literal: Ziwen became chief minister, thrice taking office and thrice leaving it; Zhan Qiu was thrice dismissed from the office of criminal judge.
translations.idiomatic: Ziwen became chief minister, taking office three times and resigning three times; Zhan Qiu was dismissed three times from the post of criminal judge.

sentences.zh: 彼塚墓已定而不改，此名位不常，何也？

translations.literal: Their tombs were already fixed and unchanged, yet name and rank were not constant—why?
translations.idiomatic: Their graves were long since fixed and never moved, yet rank and fortune kept changing—why?

sentences.zh: 故知榮辱升降，事關諸人，而不由於葬，六也。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that honor and disgrace, rise and fall, depend on the man and not on burial—the sixth point.
translations.idiomatic: Honor and shame, rise and fall, belong to the living—not to the tomb. That is the sixth point.

sentences.zh: 世之人為葬巫所欺，忘擗踴荼毒，以期徼幸。

translations.literal: Men of the age are deceived by burial shamans, forgetting breast-beating and the bitterness of mourning, hoping for mere luck.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the age let burial shamans deceive them, forgetting the grief of breast-beating and mourning, all for a stroke of luck.

sentences.zh: 由是相塋隴，希官爵；

translations.literal: Hence they inspect grave mounds, hoping for office and rank;
translations.idiomatic: So they inspect grave mounds, hoping for office and rank;

sentences.zh: 擇日時，規財利。

translations.literal: they select days and hours, scheming for wealth and profit.
translations.idiomatic: they choose days and hours, scheming for wealth and profit.

sentences.zh: 謂辰日不哭，欣然而受吊；

translations.literal: They say that on certain days one must not weep, and gladly accept condolences;
translations.idiomatic: They say one must not weep on certain days and accept condolences with cheer;

sentences.zh: 謂同屬不得臨壙，吉服避送其親。

translations.literal: they say that men of the same clan may not approach the grave, and in auspicious dress avoid escorting their kin.
translations.idiomatic: they say clansmen may not approach the grave and, in festive dress, shun escorting their own dead.

sentences.zh: 詭斁禮俗，不可以法，七也。

translations.literal: They pervert and ruin custom and rite and cannot serve as law—the seventh point.
translations.idiomatic: They twist and ruin custom and rite and cannot stand as law—that is the seventh point.

sentences.zh: 帝又詔造《方域圖》及教飛騎戰陣圖，屢稱旨。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered him to compile the Territorial Atlas and to teach the battle formations of the Flying Cavalry; he repeatedly won praise for meeting the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered him to compile the Territorial Atlas and to instruct the court in Flying Cavalry battle formations; again and again his work pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 擢太常丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 麟德中，以太子司更大夫卒。

translations.literal: In the Linde era he died while serving as Grand Master of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: During the Linde reign he died in office as Grand Master of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 生平豫修書及著述甚多。

translations.literal: In life he took part in compiling many books and wrote extensively.
translations.idiomatic: In life he helped compile many books and wrote a great deal.

sentences.zh: 子 方毅子方毅，七歲能誦經。

translations.literal: His son was Fang Yi; at seven he could recite the classics.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fang Yi could recite the classics at the age of seven.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞其敏，召見，奇之，賜束帛。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong heard of his quickness, summoned him, marveled at him, and bestowed silks.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong heard how bright he was, he summoned the boy, was struck by his talent, and granted him silks.

sentences.zh: 長為右衛鎧曹參軍。

translations.literal: When grown, he served as Staff Officer of the Armor Bureau in the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he served as Staff Officer of the Armor Bureau in the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 母喪，以毀卒。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death, he died from grief-exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he wasted away in mourning and died.

sentences.zh: 布車從母葬，通人郎余令以白粥、玄酒、生芻祭路隅，世共哀之。

translations.literal: With a cloth-covered cart he followed his stepmother to burial; the common man Lang Yuling offered white porridge, dark wine, and fresh grass to sacrifice at a roadside corner; the age together mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his stepmother to the grave in a simple cloth-covered cart; the commoner Lang Yuling laid out white porridge, unmixed wine, and fresh grass at a roadside corner as an offering, and all who heard of it grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 陳子昂陳子昂，字伯玉，梓州射洪人。

translations.literal: Chen Zi'ang, Chen Zi'ang, styled Boyu, was a native of Shehong in Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zi'ang, styled Boyu, was a native of Shehong in Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 其先居新城，六世祖太樂，當齊時。

translations.literal: His ancestors lived in Xincheng; his sixth-generation ancestor Tai Yue lived during the Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had settled in Xincheng; his sixth-generation ancestor Tai Yue lived under the Qi.

sentences.zh: 兄弟競豪傑，梁武帝命為郡司馬。

translations.literal: His brothers rivaled one another as bold heroes; Emperor Wu of Liang appointed him Commandant of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers competed in bold spirit; Emperor Wu of Liang appointed him Commandant of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 父元敬，世高貲，歲饑，出粟萬石賑鄉里。

translations.literal: His father Yuanjing was wealthy for generations; in a year of famine he distributed ten thousand shi of grain to relieve the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanjing came from a wealthy family; when famine struck, he gave ten thousand shi of grain to relieve the neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 舉明經，調文林郎。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed Gentleman of the Forest of Letters.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination and was posted as Gentleman of the Forest of Letters.

sentences.zh: 子昂十八未知書，以富家子，尚氣決，弋博自如。

translations.literal: At eighteen Zi'ang did not yet know books; as a rich man's son he prized bold spirit and gambled and shot at will.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen Zi'ang was still unlettered; as a rich man's son he valued daring, and he gambled and hunted as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 它日入鄉校，感悔，即痛修飭。

translations.literal: One day he entered the district school, felt remorse, and at once applied himself sternly to reform.
translations.idiomatic: One day he entered the district school, was seized with regret, and threw himself into rigorous self-reform.

sentences.zh: 文明初，舉進士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wensite era he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Wensite reign he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 時高宗崩，將遷梓宮長安，於是，關中無歲，子昂盛言東都勝塏，可營山陵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong died and the coffin was to be moved to Chang'an, Guanzhong had suffered year after year without harvest; Zi'ang forcefully argued that the Eastern Capital's terrain was superior and that the imperial tomb could be built there.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong died and the imperial coffin was to be taken to Chang'an, Guanzhong had known famine year after year; Zi'ang argued at length that the Eastern Capital offered better ground and that the tomb should be built there.

sentences.zh: 上書曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 「臣聞秦據咸陽，漢都長安，山河為固，而天下服者，以北假胡、宛之利，南資巴、蜀之饒，轉關東之粟，而收山西之寶，長羈利策，橫制宇宙。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that Qin held Xianyang and Han made Chang'an its capital; with mountains and rivers as defenses, the reason the realm submitted was that to the north they relied on the profits of Beijia Hu and Wan, to the south they drew on the riches of Ba and Shu, they transported grain from east of the Pass, and gathered the treasures of the lands west of the mountains, long holding profitable policies and controlling the universe horizontally.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that Qin held Xianyang and Han made Chang'an its capital; protected by mountains and rivers, they ruled the realm because they drew northern profit from Beijia Hu and Wan, southern wealth from Ba and Shu, shipped grain from east of the Pass, and gathered the treasures of the western lands—holding profitable leverage and commanding the world.

sentences.zh: 今則不然，燕、代迫匈奴，巴、隴嬰吐蕃，西老千里贏糧，北丁十五乘塞，歲月奔命，秦之首尾不完，所餘獨三輔間耳。

translations.literal: Now it is not so: Yan and Dai press against the Xiongnu; Ba and Long are besieged by Tibet; in the west old men carry grain for a thousand li; in the north lads of fifteen man the frontier; month after month they race to their posts—the head and tail of Qin are no longer whole, and all that remains is the region between the three metropolitan areas.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is otherwise: Yan and Dai face the Xiongnu; Ba and Long are hemmed in by Tibet; in the west old men haul grain a thousand li; in the north boys of fifteen garrison the frontier; month after month men race to their posts—the extremities of the Qin lands are broken off, and only the three metropolitan districts remain intact.

sentences.zh: 頃遭荒饉，百姓薦饑，薄河而右，惟有赤地；

translations.literal: Recently there has been famine; the people have repeatedly suffered hunger; south of the Yellow River there is only bare earth;
translations.idiomatic: Famine has struck recently; the people have gone hungry again and again; south of the Yellow River there is nothing but bare ground;

sentences.zh: 循隴以北，不逢青草。

translations.literal: Following Long northward, one does not encounter green grass.
translations.idiomatic: Travel north along Long and you find no green grass.

sentences.zh: 父兄轉徙，妻子流離。

translations.literal: Fathers and elder brothers have been displaced; wives and children scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Fathers and elder brothers have been driven from place to place; wives and children have been torn apart.

sentences.zh: 賴天悔禍，去年薄稔，羸耗之餘，幾不沉命。

translations.literal: Thanks to Heaven's regret of calamity, last year brought a scant harvest; after weakness and exhaustion, they barely escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven relented from disaster, and last year brought a thin harvest; after wasting and exhaustion, the people barely clung to life.

sentences.zh: 然流亡未還，白骨縱橫，阡陌無主，至於蓄積，猶可哀傷。

translations.literal: Yet refugees have not returned; bleached bones lie scattered; fields have no owners—and as for stored grain, the scene is still pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: Yet refugees have not come home; bleached bones lie everywhere; fields stand without owners—and even what grain remains in store is a sorrow to behold.

sentences.zh: 陛下以先帝遺意，方大駕長驅，按節西京，千乘萬騎，何從仰給？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, following the late emperor's last wishes, is about to drive the imperial procession west to Chang'an—how are thousands of chariots and ten thousand horsemen to be supplied?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, honoring the late emperor's final wishes, is about to lead the great procession west to Chang'an—where will supplies come from for thousands of chariots and myriads of horsemen?

sentences.zh: 山陵穿復，必資徒役，率臒弊之眾，興數萬之軍，調發近畿，督抶稚老，鏟山輦石，驅以就功，春作無時，何望有秋？

translations.literal: Digging and restoring the mountain tomb will require conscript labor; leading emaciated masses, raising armies of tens of thousands, mobilizing the near capital regions, driving the young and old with whips, cutting mountains and hauling stone, driving them to completion—with no season for spring planting, how can one hope for autumn harvest?
translations.idiomatic: Excavating and rebuilding the mountain tomb will demand forced labor; leading exhausted masses, raising armies in the tens of thousands, mobilizing the capital districts, whipping young and old to cut hills and haul stone and drive the work to completion—with no time left for spring planting, what hope is there of an autumn harvest?

sentences.zh: 雕氓遺噍，再罹艱苦，有不堪其困，則逸為盜賊，揭梃叫呼，可不深圖哉！

translations.literal: The battered people, left with mere scraps, suffer hardship again; those who cannot bear the distress will flee and become bandits, brandishing clubs and shouting—should this not be deeply considered!
translations.idiomatic: The worn-out people, barely surviving on scraps, would suffer hardship again; those who could not endure would break away as bandits, brandishing clubs and crying out—should this not be weighed with the utmost care!

sentences.zh: 且天子以四海為家，舜葬蒼梧，禹葬會稽，豈愛夷裔而鄙中國耶？

translations.literal: Moreover, the Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his home; Shun was buried at Cangwu and Yu at Kuaiji—did they favor barbarian lands and scorn China?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Son of Heaven makes the four seas his home; Shun was buried at Cangwu and Yu at Kuaiji—did they love foreign lands and despise the heartland?

sentences.zh: 示無外也。

translations.literal: It showed that they made no distinction between inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: It showed that they drew no line between center and periphery.

sentences.zh: 周平王、漢光武都洛，而山陵寢廟並在西土者，實以時有不可，故遺小存大，去禍取福也。

translations.literal: King Ping of Zhou and Emperor Guangwu of Han both established their capitals at Luoyang, yet their tombs and ancestral temples remained in the western lands—this was because circumstances at the time made it impossible; they therefore left the lesser and kept the greater, shunning calamity to take blessing.
translations.idiomatic: King Ping of Zhou and Emperor Guangwu of Han both ruled from Luoyang, yet their tombs and ancestral temples stood in the west—because the times made it impossible to do otherwise; they kept the greater good and set aside the lesser, turning from disaster toward blessing.

sentences.zh: 今景山崇秀，北對嵩、邙，右眄汝、海，祝融、太昊之故墟在焉。

translations.literal: Today Jingshan rises lofty and fine; to the north it faces Song and Mang; to the right it looks toward Ru and the sea; the ancient sites of Zhurong and Taihao lie there.
translations.idiomatic: Today Jingshan stands tall and splendid; to the north it faces Mount Song and Mount Mang; to the right it overlooks the Ru River and the sea; the ancient grounds of Zhurong and Taihao lie there.

sentences.zh: 園陵之美，復何以加？

translations.literal: What could add to the beauty of an imperial park and tomb?
translations.idiomatic: What could surpass the beauty of an imperial park and tomb there?

sentences.zh: 且太原廥巨萬之倉，洛口儲天下之粟，乃欲舍而不顧，儻鼠竊狗盜，西入陝郊，東犯虎牢。

translations.literal: Moreover, Taiyuan has granaries storing tens of thousands; Luokou holds the empire's grain—yet you would abandon these. Suppose petty thieves break in from the west at Shaan and strike east at Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Taiyuan keeps granaries filled with tens of thousands of measures, and Luokou stores the empire's grain—yet you would leave them unattended. Suppose common thieves slipped in from Shaan in the west and struck east at Hulao.

sentences.zh: 取敖倉一抔粟，陛下何與遏之？

translations.literal: and took a single scoop of grain from Aocang—how could Your Majesty stop them?
translations.idiomatic: If rebels scooped up a handful of grain from Aocang, how could Your Majesty prevent it?

sentences.zh: 武后奇其才，召見金華殿。

translations.literal: Empress Wu marveled at his talent and summoned him to an audience in the Jinhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was struck by his talent and summoned him to audience in the Jinhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 子昂貌柔野，少威儀，而占對慷慨，擢麟台正字。

translations.literal: Zi'ang's appearance was gentle and rustic, with little bearing of dignity, yet in answering he was ardent and impassioned; he was promoted to Correcter of the Forest Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Zi'ang looked mild and rough, with little courtly bearing, yet his replies were bold and impassioned; he was promoted to Correcter of the Forest Terrace.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，詔問群臣「調元氣當以何道？」

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chuigong era, an edict asked the ministers, "By what method should primordial qi be harmonized?"
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Chuigong reign, an edict asked the ministers, "By what means should primordial qi be harmonized?"

sentences.zh: 子昂因是勸後興明堂、大學，即上言：

translations.literal: Zi'ang thereupon urged the Empress to raise the Bright Hall and Imperial Academy, and submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Zi'ang then urged the Empress to restore the Bright Hall and the Imperial Academy, and submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞之于師曰：「元氣，天地之始，萬物之祖，王政之大端也。

translations.literal: Your subject heard from his teacher: "Primordial qi is the beginning of Heaven and Earth, the ancestor of the ten thousand things, and the great foundation of royal government.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject heard from his teacher: "Primordial qi is the origin of Heaven and Earth, the source of the ten thousand things, and the great root of royal government.

sentences.zh: 天地莫大于陰陽，萬物莫靈于人，王政莫先于安人。

translations.literal: Nothing in Heaven and Earth is greater than yin and yang; nothing among the ten thousand things is more spiritual than man; nothing in royal government comes before securing the people.
translations.idiomatic: In Heaven and Earth nothing is greater than yin and yang; among the ten thousand things nothing is more vital than man; in royal government nothing comes before settling the people.

sentences.zh: 故人安則陰陽和，陰陽和則天地平，天地平則元氣正。

translations.literal: When the people are secure, yin and yang are harmonized; when yin and yang are harmonized, Heaven and Earth are balanced; when Heaven and Earth are balanced, primordial qi is rectified.
translations.idiomatic: When the people are at peace, yin and yang are in harmony; when yin and yang are in harmony, Heaven and Earth are level; when Heaven and Earth are level, primordial qi is set right.

sentences.zh: 先王以人之通於天也，於是養成群生，順天德，使人樂其業，甘其食，美其服，然後天瑞降，地符升，風雨時，草木茂遂。

translations.literal: The former kings, because man communicates with Heaven, nourished all living beings, followed Heaven's virtue, and made men delight in their work, relish their food, and take pride in their dress—then heavenly portents descended, earthly talismans arose, wind and rain came in season, and grasses and trees flourished.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings, knowing that man communes with Heaven, nourished all living things, followed Heaven's virtue, and let people take joy in their work, relish their food, and be proud of their dress—then heavenly omens appeared, earthly signs rose up, wind and rain came in season, and grass and trees flourished.

sentences.zh: 故顓頊、唐、虞不敢荒寧，其《書》曰：「百姓昭明，協和萬邦，黎人于變時雍。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhuanxu, Tang, and Yu dared not waste their time in idleness; the Book says: "The common people were enlightened; all states were harmonized; the black-haired people were transformed until they became perfectly harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Zhuanxu, Tang, and Yu dared not neglect their duties; the Book says: "The common people were enlightened; the myriad states were brought into harmony; the people were transformed until all was tranquil.

sentences.zh: 乃命羲和，欽若昊天，曆象日月星辰，敬授人時。」

translations.literal: He then appointed Xi and He, reverently conforming to vast Heaven, to calculate and image the sun, moon, stars, and constellations, and reverently grant the seasons to the people."
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Xi and He, in reverent accord with vast Heaven, to measure and chart the sun, moon, stars, and constellations, and reverently set the seasons for the people."

sentences.zh: 和之得也。

translations.literal: This was harmony achieved.
translations.idiomatic: That was harmony attained.

sentences.zh: 夏、商之衰，桀、紂昏暴，陰陽乖行，天地震怒，山川神鬼，發妖見災，疾疫大興，終以滅亡，和之失也。

translations.literal: In the decline of Xia and Shang, Jie and Zhou were benighted and violent; yin and yang went contrary; Heaven and Earth shook with anger; mountains, rivers, spirits, and ghosts sent prodigies and showed disasters; pestilence rose greatly—and they ended in extinction; this was harmony lost.
translations.idiomatic: In the decline of Xia and Shang, Jie and Zhou were dark and brutal; yin and yang fell out of step; Heaven and Earth trembled in wrath; mountains, rivers, spirits, and ghosts sent omens and disasters; pestilence spread widely—and at last they perished; that was harmony lost.

sentences.zh: 迨周文、武創業，誠信忠厚加于百姓，故成、康刑措四十餘年，天人方和。

translations.literal: By the time of King Wen and King Wu founding their enterprise, sincerity, trust, and generous loyalty were added to the people; therefore under Cheng and Kang punishments were unused for more than forty years, and Heaven and man were then in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: When Kings Wen and Wu founded their rule, sincerity, trust, and generous loyalty were shown to the people; under Cheng and Kang punishments went unused for more than forty years, and Heaven and man were then in harmony.

sentences.zh: 而幽、厲亂常，苛慝暴虐，詬黷天地，川塚沸崩，人用愁怨。

translations.literal: But You and Li perverted the constants, were harsh, cruel, and tyrannical, insulted and defiled Heaven and Earth; streams and tombs boiled and collapsed; the people were filled with grief and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: But You and Li overturned the norms, were harsh, cruel, and oppressive, and insulted Heaven and Earth; rivers boiled and tombs collapsed; the people were steeped in grief and resentment.

sentences.zh: 其《詩》曰：「昊天不惠，降此大戾」，不先不後，為虐為瘵，顧不哀哉！

translations.literal: The Odes say: "Vast Heaven is not kind and sends down this great affliction"—neither before nor after, they made suffering and wasting sickness—how pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: "Great Heaven is unkind and sends down this great calamity"—neither early nor late, they brought torment and wasting sickness—how lamentable!
