sentences.zh: 近隋煬帝恃四海之富，鑿渠決河，自伊、洛屬之揚州，疲生人之力，泄天地之藏，中國之難起，故身死人手，宗廟為墟。

translations.literal: Recently Emperor Yang of Sui, relying on the wealth of the four seas, dug canals and cut through rivers from Yi and Luo to Yangzhou, exhausting the strength of the living, draining the stores of Heaven and Earth—then troubles arose within China; therefore he died at another's hands and his ancestral temple became ruins.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago Emperor Yang of Sui, trusting in the wealth of the four seas, dug canals and cut rivers from Yi and Luo all the way to Yangzhou, exhausting the living and draining Heaven and Earth's stores—then rebellion rose within China; he died by another's hand and his ancestral temple was reduced to ruins.

sentences.zh: 逆元氣之理也。

translations.literal: This violated the principle of primordial qi.
translations.idiomatic: That was a violation of the principle of primordial qi.

sentences.zh: 臣觀禍亂之動，天人之際，先師之說，昭然著明，不可欺也。

translations.literal: Your subject observes that when calamity and disorder stir, at the boundary between Heaven and man, the doctrine of the former masters is clearly manifest and cannot be deceived.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject sees that when calamity and disorder move, at the juncture of Heaven and man, the teaching of the former masters stands plainly revealed and cannot be denied.

sentences.zh: 陛下含天地之德，日月之明，眇然遠思，欲求太和，此伏羲氏所以為三皇首也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty embodies the virtue of Heaven and Earth and the radiance of sun and moon; with far-reaching thought you seek great harmony—this is why Fuxi was foremost among the Three Sovereigns.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty holds the virtue of Heaven and Earth and the brightness of sun and moon; with far-sighted intent you seek supreme harmony—this is why Fuxi stood first among the Three Sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 昔者，天皇大帝攬元符，東封太山，然未建明堂，享上帝，使萬世鴻業闕而不昭，殆留此盛德，以發揮陛下哉！

translations.literal: In former times the Heavenly Sovereign gathered the mandate, performed the eastern feng at Mount Tai—yet he did not build the Bright Hall or sacrifice to the Supreme Lord, leaving the grand enterprise of ten thousand generations incomplete and unrevealed—perhaps he reserved this supreme virtue to be fulfilled by Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: In former times the Heavenly Sovereign received the mandate and performed the eastern feng at Mount Tai—yet he did not build the Bright Hall or sacrifice to the Supreme Lord, leaving the great enterprise of ten thousand generations unfinished and unrevealed—perhaps he kept this supreme merit for Your Majesty to fulfill!

sentences.zh: 臣謂和元氣，睦人倫，舍此則無以為也。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that harmonizing primordial qi and cherishing human relations—apart from this there is nothing to be done.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject believes that harmonizing primordial qi and nurturing human relations—without these there is nothing worth doing.

sentences.zh: 昔黃帝合宮，有虞總期，堯衢室，夏世室，皆所以調元氣，治陰陽也。

translations.literal: In former times the Yellow Emperor had the Hall of Union, Shun the Hall of Total Governance, Yao the Crossroads Chamber, and Xia the Chamber of Generations—all to harmonize primordial qi and govern yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Yellow Emperor had the Hall of Union, Shun the Hall of Total Governance, Yao the Crossroads Chamber, and the Xia the Chamber of Generations—all to harmonize primordial qi and regulate yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 臣聞明堂有天地之制，陰陽之統，二十四氣、八風、十二月、四時、五行、二十八宿，莫不率備。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the Bright Hall embodies the pattern of Heaven and Earth and the governing principle of yin and yang—the twenty-four qi, eight winds, twelve months, four seasons, five phases, and twenty-eight lodges are all fully represented.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that the Bright Hall holds the design of Heaven and Earth and the governing thread of yin and yang—the twenty-four qi, eight winds, twelve months, four seasons, five phases, and twenty-eight lodges are all fully embodied.

sentences.zh: 王者政失則災，政順則祥。

translations.literal: When a king's government fails, disaster follows; when it is correct, auspicious signs appear.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler's government goes wrong, disaster follows; when it is right, good omens appear.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下為唐恢萬世之業，相國南郊，建明堂，與天下更始，按《周禮》、《月令》而成之。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty, to restore Tang's enterprise for ten thousand generations, to sacrifice at the southern suburb on the state's behalf, build the Bright Hall, and make a new beginning with the realm—completing it according to the Rites of Zhou and Monthly Ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject wishes Your Majesty, for Tang to restore an enterprise lasting ten thousand generations, to take the southern suburb rite as the state's model, build the Bright Hall, and begin anew with the realm—completing it according to the Rites of Zhou and the Monthly Ordinances.

sentences.zh: 乃月孟春，乘鸞輅，駕蒼龍，朝在三公、九卿、大夫于青陽左個，負斧扆，馮玉幾，聽天下之政。

translations.literal: Then in the first month of spring, riding the phoenix carriage and driving the azure dragon, holding court with the Three Excellencies, Nine Ministers, and grand masters at the Left Alcove of Qingyang, leaning on the axe-screen and seated before the jade armrest, listening to the governance of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Then in the first month of spring, riding the phoenix carriage and driving the azure dragon, holding court with the Three Excellencies, Nine Ministers, and grandees at the Left Alcove of Qingyang, leaning on the axe-screen and seated before the jade armrest, hearing the governance of the realm.

sentences.zh: 躬藉田、親蠶以勸農桑，養三老、五更以教孝悌，明訟恤獄以息淫刑，脩文德以止干戈，察孝廉以除貪吏。

translations.literal: Personally performing the plowing rite and tending silkworms to encourage farming and sericulture; supporting the Three Elders and Five Worthies to teach filial piety and brotherliness; clarifying lawsuits and pitying prisoners to end excessive punishments; cultivating civil virtue to stop warfare; examining Filial and Incorrupt candidates to remove greedy officials.
translations.idiomatic: Personally plowing the sacred field and tending silkworms to encourage farming and sericulture; supporting the Three Elders and Five Worthies to teach filial piety and brotherly duty; clarifying lawsuits and showing mercy in prisons to end excessive punishment; cultivating civil virtue to halt warfare; examining Filial and Incorrupt candidates to remove corrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 後宮非妃嬪禦女者，出之；

translations.literal: Those in the inner palace who are not consorts or palace attendants shall be sent out;
translations.idiomatic: Women in the inner palace who are not consorts or palace attendants should be sent away;

sentences.zh: 珠玉錦繡、雕琢伎巧無益者，棄之；

translations.literal: Pearls, jade, brocades, carved trifles, and useless craft shall be discarded;
translations.idiomatic: Pearls, jade, brocades, carved ornaments, and useless crafts should be cast aside;

sentences.zh: 巫鬼淫祀營惑於人者，禁之。

translations.literal: Wizards, ghosts, licentious sacrifices, and practices that delude the people shall be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Shamans, ghost cults, improper sacrifices, and practices that mislead the people should be banned.

sentences.zh: 臣謂不數期且見太平雲。

translations.literal: Your subject believes that within not many periods one will see the clouds of great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject believes that before long the clouds of great peace will appear.

sentences.zh: 又言：

translations.literal: He also said:
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote:

sentences.zh: 陛下方興大化，而太學久廢，堂皇埃蕪，《詩》、《書》不聞，明詔尚未及之，愚臣所以私恨也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is just launching great transformation, yet the Imperial Academy has long lain abandoned; its halls are dusty and overgrown; the Odes and Documents are no longer heard; the bright edicts have not yet reached this matter—the reason your foolish subject privately grieves.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is launching great reform, yet the Imperial Academy has long stood abandoned; its halls are dusty and overgrown; the Odes and Documents are no longer heard in them; the bright edicts have not yet touched this matter—the reason your humble subject grieves in private.

sentences.zh: 太學者，政教之地也，君臣上下之取則也，俎豆揖讓之所興也，天子于此得賢臣焉。

translations.literal: The Imperial Academy is the seat of government and teaching, the standard for ruler and subject above and below, the place where sacrificial vessels and bowing and yielding are honored—the Son of Heaven there gains worthy ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Academy is the ground of government and teaching, the measure for ruler and subject, high and low, the place where ritual vessels and courteous yielding are cultivated—the Son of Heaven there finds worthy ministers.

sentences.zh: 今委而不論，雖欲睦人倫，興治綱，失之本而求之末，不可得也。

translations.literal: Now it is left aside without discussion; though one wishes to cherish human relations and raise the bonds of governance, losing the root and seeking the branch—this cannot be attained.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is set aside without debate; though one wishes to nurture human relations and strengthen the bonds of rule, to lose the root and chase the branch is to seek what cannot be found.

sentences.zh: 「君子三年不為禮，禮必壞，三年不為樂，樂必崩」，奈何為天下而輕禮樂哉？

translations.literal: "If a gentleman goes three years without performing ritual, ritual must crumble; three years without music, music must collapse"—how can one lightly treat ritual and music while governing the realm?
translations.idiomatic: "If a gentleman goes three years without performing ritual, ritual must decay; three years without music, music must collapse"—how can one treat ritual and music lightly while governing the realm?

sentences.zh: 願引胄子使歸太學，國家之大務不可廢已。

translations.literal: I wish that sons of officials be recalled to the Imperial Academy—this great affair of state must not be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that sons of officials be brought back to the Imperial Academy—this great business of state must not be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 後召見，賜筆劄中書省，令條上利害。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned to audience; writing materials at the Secretariat were granted him, and he was ordered to set forth benefits and harms in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned to audience; the Secretariat granted him writing materials and ordered him to list benefits and harms in detail.

sentences.zh: 子昂對三事。

translations.literal: Zi'ang answered on three matters.
translations.idiomatic: Zi'ang responded on three points.

sentences.zh: 其一言：

translations.literal: The first stated:
translations.idiomatic: The first point read:

sentences.zh: 九道出大使巡按天下，申黜陟，求人瘼，臣謂計有未盡也。

translations.literal: Nine routes dispatched envoys to inspect the realm, proclaim promotions and demotions, and seek the people's afflictions—your subject believes the plan is not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: Nine routes sent out envoys to tour the realm, announce promotions and demotions, and seek the people's hardships—your subject believes the plan still falls short.

sentences.zh: 且陛下發使，必欲使百姓知天子夙夜憂勤之也，群臣知考績而任之也，奸暴不逞知將除之也，則莫如擇仁可以恤孤、明可以振滯、剛不避強禦、智足以照奸者，然後以為使，故輶軒未動，而天下翹然待之矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Your Majesty sends envoys, you surely wish the people to know the Son of Heaven's early and late anxiety and diligence, the ministers to know they will be assessed and entrusted by merit, and the wicked and violent to know they will be removed—then nothing is better than choosing men who are benevolent enough to comfort the orphaned, clear-sighted enough to revive the stagnant, firm enough not to shun the powerful, and wise enough to expose wickedness—and only then appointing them as envoys; thus before the inspection carriages move, the realm will look up eagerly in anticipation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when Your Majesty sends envoys, you surely want the people to know the Son of Heaven's sleepless diligence, the ministers to know they will be judged and entrusted by merit, and the wicked and violent to know they will be removed—then nothing is better than choosing men benevolent enough to comfort the orphaned, clear enough to revive the neglected, firm enough not to shrink from the powerful, and wise enough to expose wrongdoing—and only then making them envoys; then before the inspection carriages even move, the realm will look up in eager expectation.

sentences.zh: 今使且未出，道路之人皆已指笑，欲望進賢下不肖，豈可得邪？

translations.literal: Now the envoys have not yet set out, yet people on the road are already pointing and laughing; to hope to promote the worthy and demote the unworthy—how can that be achieved?
translations.idiomatic: Now the envoys have not yet departed, yet travelers are already pointing and laughing; to hope thereby to promote the worthy and demote the unworthy—how can that be done?

sentences.zh: 宰相奉詔書，有遣使之名，無任使之實。

translations.literal: The chancellor receives the edict—there is the name of dispatching envoys, but not the reality of entrusting them.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor receives the edict—there is the title of sending envoys, but not the substance of entrusting them.

sentences.zh: 使愈出，天下愈弊，徒令百姓治道路，送往迎來，不見其益也。

translations.literal: The more envoys sent out, the more the realm is worn down; it only makes the people repair roads and send off and welcome arrivals, without visible benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The more envoys go out, the more the realm is worn down; it only makes the people repair roads and escort arrivals and departures, with no visible gain.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下更選有威重風概為眾推者，因御前殿，以使者之禮禮之，諄諄戒敕所以出使之意，乃授以節。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty to choose anew men of authority, weight, and bearing whom the masses recommend; in the imperial front hall, treat them with the ritual due envoys; earnestly admonish them on the intent of the mission; then confer upon them credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject asks Your Majesty to choose anew men of authority, presence, and reputation whom the people respect; in the imperial front hall, receive them with the rites due envoys; earnestly instruct them in the purpose of the mission; then grant them credentials.

sentences.zh: 自京師及州縣，登拔才良，求人瘼，宣佈上意，令若家見而戶曉。

translations.literal: From the capital to prefectures and counties, promote the talented and good, seek the people's afflictions, proclaim the sovereign's intent, making orders as if seen in every home and understood at every door.
translations.idiomatic: From the capital down to prefectures and counties, they should promote the talented and worthy, seek the people's hardships, and proclaim the sovereign's intent, so that orders seem seen in every home and understood at every door.

sentences.zh: 昔堯、舜不下席而化天下，蓋黜陟幽明能折衷者。

translations.literal: In old times Yao and Shun transformed the realm without leaving their mats—because promotion and demotion of the obscure and the clear could strike the balance.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Yao and Shun transformed the realm without leaving their seats—because they could weigh promotion and demotion of the obscure and the clear and strike the balance.

sentences.zh: 陛下知難得人，則不如少出使。

translations.literal: Your Majesty knows worthy men are hard to find—then it would be better to send out fewer envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty knows worthy men are hard to find—then it would be better to send out fewer envoys.

sentences.zh: 彼煩數而無益於化，是烹小鮮而數撓之矣。

translations.literal: That frequent dispatch is of no benefit to transformation is like cooking a small fish and repeatedly stirring it.
translations.idiomatic: To send them out again and again without benefit to reform is like cooking a small fish and stirring it repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 其二言：

translations.literal: The second stated:
translations.idiomatic: The second point read:

sentences.zh: 刺史、縣令，政教之首。

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates are the heads of government and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates stand at the head of government and teaching.

sentences.zh: 陛下布德澤，下詔書，必待刺史、縣令謹宣而奉行之。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty spreads gracious favor and issues edicts, it must wait for prefects and magistrates carefully to proclaim and carry them out.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty spreads gracious favor and issues edicts, they must wait for prefects and magistrates to proclaim and carry them out faithfully.

sentences.zh: 不得其人，則委棄有司，掛牆屋耳，百姓安得知之？

translations.literal: If the right men are not obtained, they are abandoned to the offices and merely hung on walls—how can the common people know of them?
translations.idiomatic: If the wrong men are appointed, the edicts are left with the offices and merely hung on walls—how can the common people ever know of them?

sentences.zh: 一州得才刺史，十萬戶賴其福；

translations.literal: If one prefecture gains a capable prefect, a hundred thousand households rely on his blessing;
translations.idiomatic: When a prefecture gets a capable prefect, a hundred thousand households share in his blessing;

sentences.zh: 得不才刺史，十萬戶受其困。

translations.literal: if it gets an incapable prefect, a hundred thousand households suffer his oppression.
translations.idiomatic: when it gets an incapable one, a hundred thousand households suffer under him.

sentences.zh: 國家興衰，在此職也。

translations.literal: The rise and fall of the state rests on this office.
translations.idiomatic: The rise and fall of the state depend on this office.

sentences.zh: 今吏部調縣令如補一尉，但計資考，不求賢良。

translations.literal: Today the Ministry of Personnel assigns magistrates as if filling a single aide's post—reckoning only seniority and assessment, not seeking the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Ministry of Personnel posts magistrates as if filling a single aide's vacancy—counting only seniority and review scores, not seeking the worthy.

sentences.zh: 有如不次用人，則天下囂然相謗矣，狃于常而不變也。

translations.literal: If anyone were promoted out of turn, the realm would clamor with mutual slander—they are wedded to routine and will not change.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone were promoted out of turn, the realm would erupt in mutual slander—they cling to routine and refuse to change.

sentences.zh: 故庸人皆任縣令，教化之陵遲，顧不甚哉！

translations.literal: Therefore mediocrities fill every magistracy—is it not obvious that education and transformation have declined!
translations.idiomatic: So mediocrities fill every magistracy—is it not plain that teaching and transformation have decayed!

sentences.zh: 其三言：

translations.literal: The third stated:
translations.idiomatic: The third point read:

sentences.zh: 天下有危機，禍福因之而生。

translations.literal: The realm has a critical pivot from which fortune and calamity arise.
translations.idiomatic: The realm has a critical pivot, and fortune and calamity spring from it.

sentences.zh: 機靜則有福，動則有禍，百姓安則樂生，不安則輕生者是也。

translations.literal: When the pivot is still, there is fortune; when it moves, calamity; when the people are secure they cherish life, when insecure they hold life cheap—such is the case.
translations.idiomatic: When the pivot stays still, fortune follows; when it moves, calamity follows; when the people are secure they value life, when insecure they treat life lightly—such is the case.

sentences.zh: 今軍旅之弊，夫妻不得安，父子不相養，五六年矣。

translations.literal: Now the harm of campaigns: husbands and wives cannot live in peace, fathers and sons cannot support one another—this has gone on five or six years.
translations.idiomatic: Now the harm of military service: husbands and wives cannot live in peace, fathers and sons cannot care for one another—and this has lasted five or six years.

sentences.zh: 自劍南盡河、隴，山東由青、徐、曹、汴，河北舉滄、瀛、趙、鄚，或困水旱，或頓兵疫，死亡流離略盡，尚賴陛下憫其失職，凡兵戍調發，一切罷之，使人得妻子相見，父兄相保，可謂能靜其機也。

translations.literal: From Jiannan to the end of He and Long, in Shandong from Qing, Xu, Cao, and Bian, across Hebei in Cang, Ying, Zhao, and Mo—some afflicted by flood and drought, some struck by military pestilence—death and flight have nearly emptied the land; yet thanks to Your Majesty's pity for their hardship, all military levies and conscriptions were abolished, letting men meet wives and children and fathers and elder brothers protect one another—this may be called stilling the pivot.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiannan through He and Long, in Shandong from Qing, Xu, Cao, and Bian, and across Hebei in Cang, Ying, Zhao, and Mo—some ravaged by flood and drought, some broken by war and pestilence—death and exile have nearly emptied the land; yet thanks to Your Majesty's pity for their plight, all military levies and conscriptions were abolished, letting men see wives and children again and fathers and elder brothers protect one another—this may be called stilling the pivot.

sentences.zh: 然臣恐將相有貪夷狄利，以廣地強武說陛下者，欲動其機，機動則禍構。

translations.literal: Yet your subject fears that generals and chancellors who greedily covet profit from the barbarians, urging Your Majesty with claims of extended territory and strengthened arms, wish to move the pivot—and when the pivot moves, calamity takes shape.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your subject fears that generals and chancellors who greedily seek profit from the barbarians, urging Your Majesty with talk of wider territory and stronger arms, will move the pivot—and when the pivot moves, calamity takes form.

sentences.zh: 宜脩文德，去刑罰，勸農桑，以息疲民。

translations.literal: One should cultivate civil virtue, remove punishments, encourage farming and sericulture, and give rest to the weary people.
translations.idiomatic: You should cultivate civil virtue, reduce punishments, encourage farming and sericulture, and give rest to the exhausted people.

sentences.zh: 蠻夷知中國有聖王，必累譯至矣。

translations.literal: When the barbarians know that China has a sage king, translations will surely arrive in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarians know that China has a sage king, envoys will surely come in endless succession.

sentences.zh: 于時，吐蕃、九姓叛，詔田揚名發金山道十姓兵討之。

translations.literal: At that time the Tibetans and the Nine Surnames rebelled; an edict ordered Tian Yangming to dispatch troops of the Ten Surnames along the Jingshan route to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Tibetans and the Nine Surnames rebelled; an edict ordered Tian Yangming to mobilize the Ten Surnames' troops on the Jingshan route to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 十姓君長以三萬騎戰，有功，遂請入朝。

translations.literal: The chieftains of the Ten Surnames fought with thirty thousand horsemen, achieved merit, and then requested to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftains of the Ten Surnames fought with thirty thousand horsemen, won distinction, and then asked to come to court.

sentences.zh: 後責其嘗不奉命擅破回紇，不聽。

translations.literal: Later they blamed him for having once disobeyed orders and attacked the Uyghurs on his own, and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the court blamed Yang Ming for having attacked the Uyghurs without authorization, and refused to heed the petition.

sentences.zh: 子昂上疏曰：

translations.literal: Zi'ang submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zi'ang submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 國家能制十姓者，繇九姓強大，臣服中國，故勢微弱，委命下吏。

translations.literal: The reason the state could control the Ten Surnames was that the Nine Surnames were powerful, submitted to China, and therefore their power was weak and they entrusted their fate to our lower officials.
translations.idiomatic: The court could control the Ten Surnames only because the Nine Surnames had been strong enough to submit to China, leaving the Ten Surnames weak and dependent on our frontier officials.

sentences.zh: 今九姓叛亡，北蕃喪亂，君長無主，回紇殘破，磧北諸姓已非國有，欲犄角亡叛，唯金山諸蕃共為形勢。

translations.literal: Now the Nine Surnames have rebelled and fled, the northern tribes are in disorder and ruin, their chieftains are without a master, the Uyghurs are broken, and the various clans north of the desert are no longer possessions of the state. If they wish to join forces with the fugitives, only the tribes of the Golden Mountain can together form a counterweight.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Nine Surnames have rebelled and scattered, the northern frontier is in chaos, tribal leaders are headless, the Uyghurs are shattered, and the peoples north of the desert no longer belong to the empire. If they mean to ally with the rebels, only the Golden Mountain tribes can still form a common front.

sentences.zh: 有司乃以揚名擅破回紇，歸十姓之罪，拒而遣還，不使入朝，恐非羈戎之長策也。

translations.literal: Yet the officials, because Yang Ming had attacked the Uyghurs on his own authority, imputed the fault to the Ten Surnames, refused them, and sent them back, not allowing them to enter court—this, I fear, is not the long-term policy for restraining the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the officials, holding Yang Ming's unauthorized attack on the Uyghurs against the Ten Surnames, turned them away and barred them from court audience—hardly a wise long-term policy for keeping the frontier tribes in hand.

sentences.zh: 夫戎有鳥獸心，親之則順，疑之則亂，今阻其善意，則十姓內無國家親信之恩，外有回紇報仇之患，懷不自安，鳥駭狼顧，則河西諸蕃自此拒命矣。

translations.literal: Barbarians have the hearts of birds and beasts: treat them kindly and they obey; suspect them and they rebel. Now, by blocking their goodwill, the Ten Surnames will have no bond of trust with the state within, and without will face the Uyghurs' vengeance. Uneasy in mind, startled like birds and glancing like wolves, the Hexi tribes from this point will refuse their orders.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians have the hearts of wild creatures: win their trust and they follow; breed suspicion and they turn violent. By rejecting their goodwill, the Ten Surnames will lose the state's favor at home and face Uyghur vengeance abroad. Restless and fearful, they will bolt like startled birds—and from that moment the Hexi tribes will refuse to obey.

sentences.zh: 且夷狄相攻，中國之福。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the barbarians attack one another, it is China's good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: When barbarians fight one another, China profits.

sentences.zh: 今回紇已破，既無可言；

translations.literal: Now the Uyghurs are already broken, and there is nothing more to be said of them;
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs are already broken; nothing more need be said of them.

sentences.zh: 十姓非罪，又不當絕。

translations.literal: the Ten Surnames are not guilty, and ought not to be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The Ten Surnames are not at fault and should not be rejected.

sentences.zh: 罪止揚名，足以慰其酋領矣。

translations.literal: Punishment need only fall on Yang Ming, enough to reassure their chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Punish Yang Ming alone, and that will be enough to satisfy their leaders.

sentences.zh: 近詔同城權置安北府，其地當磧南口，制匈奴之沖，常為劇鎮。

translations.literal: A recent edict provisionally established the Protectorate of Pacified North at Tongcheng; its site lies at the southern mouth of the desert, commanding the route against the Xiongnu, and it will always be a critical garrison.
translations.idiomatic: A recent edict provisionally established the Anbei Protectorate at Tongcheng, at the desert's southern gateway—the choke point against the northern nomads and a post that will always be critical.

sentences.zh: 臣頃聞磧北突厥之歸者已千餘帳，來者未止，甘州降戶四千帳，亦置同城。

translations.literal: Your servant has lately heard that more than a thousand tents of Turks returning from north of the desert have already arrived, and newcomers have not ceased; four thousand tents of surrendered households from Ganzhou were also placed at Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately heard that more than a thousand tents of Turks returning from north of the desert have already arrived, with more still coming, and four thousand tents of surrendered households from Ganzhou were also settled at Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 今磧北喪亂、荒饉之餘，無所存仰，陛下開府招納，誠覆全戎狄之仁也。

translations.literal: Now, in the aftermath of disorder and famine north of the desert, they have nothing on which to rely. Your Majesty opens a protectorate to receive them—truly the benevolence that shelters and preserves the barbarians whole.
translations.idiomatic: North of the desert lies only ruin and famine; these people have nowhere to turn. In opening a protectorate to receive them, Your Majesty shows the benevolence that truly shelters the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 然同城本無儲峙，而降附蕃落不免寒饑，更相劫掠。

translations.literal: Yet Tongcheng originally had no stored provisions, and the surrendered tribal peoples could not escape cold and hunger, so they plundered one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: But Tongcheng had no stores to begin with, and the surrendered tribes could not escape hunger and cold, so they began raiding one another.

sentences.zh: 今安北有官牛羊六千，粟麥萬斛，城孤兵少，降者日眾，不加救恤，盜劫日多。

translations.literal: Now at Anbei there are six thousand government cattle and sheep and ten thousand bushels of grain and wheat; the city is isolated and the garrison small, while the surrendered increase daily. Without relief, robbery grows daily.
translations.idiomatic: Anbei now holds six thousand government cattle and sheep and ten thousand bushels of grain, yet the city is isolated, the garrison is small, and surrendered tribes arrive daily. Without relief, theft and plunder multiply by the day.

sentences.zh: 夫人情以求生為急，今有粟麥牛羊為之餌，而不救其死，安得不為盜乎？

translations.literal: Human feeling urgently seeks survival. Now there is grain, wheat, cattle, and sheep to serve as bait, yet their deaths are not relieved—how can they fail to become robbers?
translations.idiomatic: Men will do anything to live. Grain, cattle, and sheep lie within reach like bait, yet no one saves them from starvation—is it any wonder they turn to banditry?

sentences.zh: 盜興則安北不全，甘、涼以往，蹺以待陷，後為邊患，禍未可量。

translations.literal: When robbery rises, Anbei cannot remain intact; from Gan and Liang onward, the frontier will wait to fall. Later it will become a border calamity, and the harm cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Once banditry spreads, Anbei cannot hold; from Ganzhou and Liangzhou westward the frontier will stand open to collapse. The border trouble that follows will be beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 是則誘使亂，誨之盜也。

translations.literal: This is to entice disorder and teach robbery.
translations.idiomatic: This is to invite chaos and teach men to steal.

sentences.zh: 且夷狄代有雄傑，與中國抗，有如勃起，招合遺散，眾將系興，此國家大機，不可失也。

translations.literal: Moreover, generation after generation the barbarians produce bold men who resist China; like a sudden rising, they gather the scattered remnants and the masses will follow. This is a great opportunity for the state and must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the barbarians produce bold leaders generation after generation who stand against China. Like a sudden uprising, one such man can rally the scattered and bind the masses to him. This is a great opening for the state and must not be missed.

sentences.zh: 又謂：

translations.literal: He also said:
translations.idiomatic: He also argued:

sentences.zh: 河西諸州，軍興以來，公私儲蓄，尤可嗟痛。

translations.literal: Since military campaigns began in the Hexi commanderies, public and private stores have been especially lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, public and private reserves across the Hexi commanderies have been shockingly depleted.

sentences.zh: 涼州歲食六萬斛，屯田所收不能償墾。

translations.literal: Liangzhou consumes sixty thousand bushels of grain yearly; what the garrison farms harvest cannot repay what was opened for cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou consumes sixty thousand bushels of grain each year, yet its garrison farms cannot recover the cost of the land they break.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲制河西，定亂戎，此州空虛，未可動也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wishes to control Hexi and settle the disorderly barbarians, this commandery is empty and cannot yet be stirred.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty means to hold Hexi and pacify the frontier tribes, this commandery is too hollow to disturb.

sentences.zh: 甘州所積四十萬斛，觀其山川，誠河西喉咽地，北當九姓，南逼吐蕃，奸回不測，伺我邊罅。

translations.literal: The stores accumulated at Ganzhou amount to four hundred thousand bushels. Observing its mountains and rivers, it is truly the throat of Hexi: to the north it faces the Nine Surnames, to the south it presses against Tibet; treacherous rebels are unpredictable and watch our border gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Ganzhou holds four hundred thousand bushels in its granaries. By its terrain it is truly the throat of Hexi: the Nine Surnames lie to the north, Tibet to the south, and restless enemies watch every gap in our defenses.

sentences.zh: 故甘州地廣粟多，左右受敵，但戶止三千，勝兵者少，屯田廣夷，倉庾豐衍，瓜、肅以西，皆仰其餫，一旬不往，士已枵饑。

translations.literal: Thus Ganzhou's land is broad and its grain abundant, yet it is threatened on both sides. Its households number only three thousand, and able soldiers are few; garrison farms stretch through barbarian lands and the granaries overflow. From Guazhou and Suzhou westward all depend on its transport—if supplies fail for ten days, the troops are already hollow with hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Ganzhou's lands are wide and its grain plentiful, yet it is menaced from both sides. It has only three thousand households and few fit for battle; its garrison farms stretch deep into tribal country and its granaries are full. From Guazhou and Suzhou westward all live on its grain—ten days without a convoy and the troops are starving.

sentences.zh: 是河西之命系于甘州矣。

translations.literal: The fate of Hexi hangs on Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi's fate hangs on Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 且其四十余屯，水泉良沃，不待天時，歲取二十萬斛，但人力寡乏，未盡墾發。

translations.literal: Moreover, its more than forty garrison farms have good water and fertile soil; without waiting on the season they harvest two hundred thousand bushels yearly, but manpower is scarce and the land is not fully opened.
translations.idiomatic: Its forty-odd garrison farms enjoy good water and rich soil; without relying on favorable seasons they yield two hundred thousand bushels a year, yet labor is too thin and much land remains unbroken.

sentences.zh: 異時吐番不敢東侵者，繇甘、涼士馬強盛，以振其入。

translations.literal: In former times Tibet did not dare invade eastward because Gan and Liang had strong soldiers and horses to check its advance.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier times Tibet did not dare strike eastward because Ganzhou and Liangzhou had strong troops and horses enough to repel any advance.

sentences.zh: 今甘州積粟萬計，兵少不足以制賊，若吐蕃敢大入，燔蓄谷，蹂諸屯，則河西諸州，我何以守？

translations.literal: Now Ganzhou's stored grain is counted by the ten thousand, yet its soldiers are too few to control the enemy. If Tibet dares a major invasion, burns the stored grain, and tramples the garrison farms, how shall we hold the Hexi commanderies?
translations.idiomatic: Ganzhou's granaries are now stocked by the ten thousand bushels, yet its garrison is too small to check the enemy. If Tibet launches a major raid, burns the stores, and destroys the farms, how will we hold Hexi?

sentences.zh: 宜益屯兵，外得以防盜，內得以營農，取數年之收，可飽士百萬，則天兵所臨，何求不得哉？

translations.literal: It is fitting to increase garrison troops: outwardly to guard against bandits, inwardly to run the farms. Take a few years' harvest and a million soldiers can be fed—then when the imperial army advances, what will it not obtain?
translations.idiomatic: Troops should be increased: outwardly to suppress raiders, inwardly to work the farms. A few years' harvest would feed a million men—then when the imperial army moves, what could it not achieve?

sentences.zh: 其後吐蕃果入寇，終後世為邊患最甚。

translations.literal: Afterward Tibet did indeed invade, and through the rest of the dynasty it was the gravest of border troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet did invade, and for the rest of the dynasty it proved the gravest border threat.

sentences.zh: 後方謀開蜀山，由雅州道翦生羌，因以襲吐蕃。

translations.literal: Later there was a plan to open the Shu mountains and, by the route through Yazhou, cut down the Raw Qiang and thereby strike Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Later officials proposed opening routes through the Shu mountains, marching by way of Yazhou to subdue the Raw Qiang and then strike Tibet.

sentences.zh: 子昂上書以七驗諫止之，曰：

translations.literal: Zi'ang submitted a memorial using seven proofs to remonstrate and stop it, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zi'ang submitted a memorial offering seven proofs against the plan, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞亂生必由於怨。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that disorder always arises from resentment.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that rebellion always springs from grievance.

sentences.zh: 雅州羌未嘗一日為盜，今無罪蒙戮，怨必甚，怨甚則蜂駭且亡，而邊邑連兵，守備不解，蜀之禍構矣。

translations.literal: The Qiang of Yazhou have never for a single day been bandits. Now, though guiltless, they face slaughter—their resentment must be extreme. Extreme resentment will startle them like swarming bees and drive them to flight, border towns will link arms in war, defenses will never stand down, and Shu will have its calamity in place.
translations.idiomatic: The Yazhou Qiang have never been bandits for a single day. Now innocent men face slaughter—their resentment will be fierce. Fierce resentment will scatter them like a disturbed hive and send them fleeing; border towns will mobilize, garrisons will never stand down, and disaster will take root in Shu.

sentences.zh: 東漢喪敗，亂始諸羌，一驗也。

translations.literal: Eastern Han fell to ruin and disorder began with the Qiang—the first proof.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han collapsed and rebellion began with the Qiang—that is the first proof.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃黠獪，抗天誅者二十餘年。

translations.literal: Tibet is cunning and has resisted Heaven's punishment for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet is cunning and has defied imperial punishment for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 前日薛仁貴、郭待封以十萬眾敗大非川，一甲不返；

translations.literal: In earlier days Xue Rengui and Guo Daifeng, with a hundred thousand men, were defeated at Da Feichuan and not a single suit of armor returned;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xue Rengui and Guo Daifeng led a hundred thousand men to defeat at Da Feichuan and not one soldier returned in armor;

sentences.zh: 李敬玄、劉審禮舉十八萬眾困青海，身執賊廷，關、隴為空。

translations.literal: Li Jingxuan and Liu Shenli, raising a hundred and eighty thousand, were trapped at Qinghai; they themselves were seized in the enemy court, and Guan and Long were emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingxuan and Liu Shenli mustered a hundred and eighty thousand men and were trapped at Qinghai; they were taken in the enemy court, and Guanzhong and Longyou were stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 今乃欲建李處一為上將，驅疲兵襲不可幸之吐蕃，舉為賊笑，二驗也。

translations.literal: Now you wish to make Li Chuyi supreme commander and drive weary troops against Tibet, which cannot be taken by luck—the whole affair will become the enemy's jest. The second proof.
translations.idiomatic: Now you would make Li Chuyi supreme commander and drive exhausted troops against Tibet when success cannot be left to chance—the whole venture will become the enemy's laughingstock. That is the second proof.

sentences.zh: 夫事有求利而得害者。

translations.literal: In affairs there are those who seek profit and obtain harm.
translations.idiomatic: Some undertakings promise profit and deliver ruin.

sentences.zh: 昔蜀與中國不通，秦以金牛、美女啖蜀侯，侯使五丁力士棧褒斜，鑿通谷，迎秦之饋。

translations.literal: In former times Shu and the central states were not connected. Qin used a golden ox and beautiful women to entice the Marquis of Shu; the marquis sent five strong men to build a plank road through Baoxie, cut open the pass, and receive Qin's provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shu and the heartland were not connected. Qin baited the Lord of Shu with a golden ox and beautiful women; the lord sent five strong men to build a plank road through Baoxie, open the pass, and receive Qin's grain.

sentences.zh: 秦隨以兵，而地入中州，三驗也。

translations.literal: Qin followed with troops, and the land entered the central domain—the third proof.
translations.idiomatic: Qin marched in after its grain, and the land passed into the central realm—that is the third proof.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃愛蜀富，思盜之矣，徒以障隊隘絕，頓餓喙不得噬。

translations.literal: Tibet covets Shu's wealth and thinks to steal it, but barrier ranges and narrow passes block the way, and it can only hunger with beak agape and cannot bite.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet covets Shu's wealth and longs to seize it, yet mountain barriers and narrow passes hold it back—it can only hunger at the gate and cannot bite.

sentences.zh: 今撤山羌，開阪險，使賊得收奔亡以攻邊，是除道待賊，舉蜀以遺之，四驗也。

translations.literal: Now, by removing the mountain Qiang and opening the pass hazards, you let the enemy gather fugitives to attack the border—this is to clear the road and wait for the bandits, handing Shu over to them. The fourth proof.
translations.idiomatic: Now, by uprooting the mountain Qiang and opening the dangerous passes, you would let the enemy rally fugitives to strike the frontier—this is to level the road for invaders and hand Shu over to them. That is the fourth proof.

sentences.zh: 蜀為西南一都會，國之寶府，又人富粟多，浮江而下，可濟中國。

translations.literal: Shu is the great metropolis of the southwest and the treasure house of the realm; its people are rich and its grain abundant, and floating down the river it can supply the central states.
translations.idiomatic: Shu is the great metropolis of the southwest and the empire's treasure house; its people are wealthy, its grain plentiful, and by river it can feed the heartland.

sentences.zh: 今圖僥倖之利，以事西羌，得羌地不足耕，得羌財不足富。

translations.literal: Now, for the sake of lucky profit, you would move against the western Qiang: Qiang land gained would not suffice to farm, Qiang wealth gained would not suffice to enrich.
translations.idiomatic: Now, chasing lucky profit, you would strike the western Qiang—yet Qiang land won would not repay cultivation, and Qiang goods won would not repay the cost.

sentences.zh: 是過殺無辜之眾，以傷陛下之仁，五驗也。

translations.literal: This is to kill the guiltless in excess and wound Your Majesty's benevolence—the fifth proof.
translations.idiomatic: This is to slaughter innocent multitudes and wound Your Majesty's benevolence—that is the fifth proof.

sentences.zh: 蜀所恃，有險也；

translations.literal: What Shu relies on is its hazards;
translations.idiomatic: Shu relies on its natural defenses;

sentences.zh: 蜀所安，無役也。

translations.literal: what Shu rests in is freedom from corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Shu rests secure because it bears no corvée.

sentences.zh: 今開蜀險，役蜀人，險開則便寇，人役則傷財。

translations.literal: Now, opening Shu's hazards and conscripting Shu men—once the hazards are opened the enemy gains ease, and once men are conscripted wealth is harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Open Shu's defenses and conscript its people—open the passes and invaders gain easy access; levy labor and wealth is drained.

sentences.zh: 臣恐未及見羌，而奸盜在其中矣。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that before the Qiang are even seen, treacherous robbers will already be among us.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that before a single Qiang is reached, treachery and plunder will already be at work among us.

sentences.zh: 異時益州長史李崇真托言吐蕃寇松州，天子為盛軍師，趣轉餉以備之。

translations.literal: In former times the Yizhou chief administrator Li Chongzhen, on false pretense that Tibet was raiding Songzhou, moved the Son of Heaven to mobilize a great army and rush transport to prepare against it.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Yizhou chief administrator Li Chongzhen falsely claimed Tibet was raiding Songzhou, moved the emperor to mobilize a great army, and rushed supplies to meet the threat.

sentences.zh: 不三年，巴、蜀大困，不見一賊，而崇真奸贓已钜萬。

translations.literal: In less than three years Ba and Shu were greatly exhausted; not a single bandit was seen, yet Chongzhen's corrupt gains already amounted to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In less than three years Ba and Shu were exhausted; not one enemy was seen, yet Chongzhen's corrupt takings already ran to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 今得非有奸臣圖利，復以生羌為資？

translations.literal: Might it not be that treacherous ministers now seek profit and again use the Raw Qiang as their resource?
translations.idiomatic: Might treacherous ministers not now be scheming for profit and again using the Raw Qiang as their pretext?

sentences.zh: 六驗也。

translations.literal: The sixth proof.
translations.idiomatic: That is the sixth proof.

sentences.zh: 蜀士尪孱不知兵，一虜持矛，百人不敢當。

translations.literal: Shu soldiers are frail and know nothing of war; one barbarian with a spear and a hundred men dare not confront him.
translations.idiomatic: Shu men are frail and untrained in war; one barbarian with a spear and a hundred Shu soldiers will not stand against him.

sentences.zh: 若西戎不即破滅，臣見蜀之邊垂且不守，而為羌夷所暴，七驗也。

translations.literal: If the western barbarians are not at once broken and destroyed, your servant sees that Shu's border will soon go undefended and be ravaged by the Qiang and the tribes—the seventh proof.
translations.idiomatic: If the western tribes are not swiftly crushed, I see Shu's frontier soon undefended and overrun by Qiang and tribal raiders—that is the seventh proof.

sentences.zh: 國家近廢安北，拔單于，棄龜茲、疏勒，天下以為務仁不務廣，務養不務殺，行太古三皇事。

translations.literal: The state has lately abolished Anbei, withdrawn the Chanyu Protectorate, and abandoned Kucha and Kashgar; the realm believes it seeks benevolence rather than expansion, nurture rather than slaughter, and acts in the manner of the Three August Ones of deepest antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The court has lately abolished Anbei, withdrawn the Chanyu Protectorate, and abandoned Kucha and Kashgar; the realm takes this as a turn toward benevolence over expansion, nurture over slaughter—the way of the ancient Three Sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 今徇貪夫之議，誅無罪之羌，遺全蜀患，此臣所未諭。

translations.literal: Now, following the counsel of greedy men, you would punish guiltless Qiang and bequeath a whole Shu to calamity—this your servant cannot understand.
translations.idiomatic: Now, heeding greedy advisers, you would punish innocent Qiang and leave all Shu exposed to disaster—this I cannot understand.

sentences.zh: 方山東饑，關隴弊，生人流亡，誠陛下寧靜思和天人之時，安可動甲兵、興大役，以自生亂？

translations.literal: Meanwhile the east is in famine, Guan and Long are exhausted, and the living flee in exile. Truly Your Majesty should think in quiet and harmonize with the season of Heaven and man—how can you stir armor and raise great works and thereby breed disorder yourselves?
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the east starves, Guanzhong and Longyou are worn out, and people flee in exile. Your Majesty should reflect in stillness and align with the harmony of Heaven and man—how can you stir armies, launch great projects, and breed rebellion at home?

sentences.zh: 又西軍失守，北屯不利，邊人駭情，今復舉輿師投不測，小人徒知議夷狄之利，非帝王至德也。

translations.literal: Moreover the western army has lost its posts and the northern garrisons fare ill; border people are terrified. Now to raise troops again and cast them into the unknown—petty men know only to debate the profit of the barbarians, not the supreme virtue of an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The western armies have lost their positions and the northern garrisons fare poorly; frontier people are terrified. To raise troops again and hurl them into the unknown—small men know only to argue the profit in barbarian wars, not the supreme virtue befitting an emperor.

sentences.zh: 善為天下者，計大而不計小，務德而不務刑，據安念危，值利思害。

translations.literal: One who governs the realm well plans for the large and not the small, pursues virtue and not punishment, holds to security and thinks of peril, meets profit and thinks of harm.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who truly governs the realm plans for the large, not the small; pursues virtue, not punishment; rests in security yet minds peril; sees profit yet weighs harm.

sentences.zh: 願陛下審計之。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to examine and calculate this carefully.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to weigh this carefully.

sentences.zh: 後復召見，使論為政之要，適時不便者，毋援上古，角空言。

translations.literal: Later he was again summoned and told to discuss the essentials of governance; where the times made something inconvenient, he was not to invoke antiquity or argue empty words.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned again and told to discuss the essentials of governance—but where the times made a point impractical, he was not to invoke antiquity or trade in empty rhetoric.

sentences.zh: 子昂乃奏八科：一措刑，二官人，三知賢，四去疑，五招諫，六勸賞，七息兵，八安宗子。

translations.literal: Zi'ang then submitted eight categories: first, easing punishments; second, appointing officials; third, knowing the worthy; fourth, removing suspicion; fifth, inviting remonstrance; sixth, encouraging reward; seventh, resting the armies; eighth, securing the imperial clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zi'ang then submitted eight proposals: easing punishments; appointing officials; recognizing talent; removing suspicion; inviting remonstrance; encouraging reward; resting the armies; and securing the imperial clansmen.

sentences.zh: 其大榷謂：

translations.literal: Their main points said:
translations.idiomatic: Their main points were these:

sentences.zh: 今百度已備，但刑急罔密，非為政之要。

translations.literal: Now the hundred offices are complete, but punishments are harsh and the net is tight—this is not the essence of governance.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred offices are now in place, yet punishments are harsh and the legal net is tight—this is not the heart of good government.

sentences.zh: 凡大人初制天下，必有凶亂叛逆之人為我驅除，以明天誅。

translations.literal: Whenever a great man first establishes the realm, there are always violent, disorderly, and rebellious men who serve as his agents of removal, to make clear Heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a founder first establishes the realm, violent and rebellious men always arise to serve as his instruments of removal, making Heaven's punishment plain.

sentences.zh: 凶叛已滅，則順人情，赦過宥罪。

translations.literal: Once the violent and rebellious are destroyed, then follow human feeling, pardon faults, and forgive crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Once the violent and rebellious are destroyed, the ruler should follow human feeling, pardon faults, and forgive crimes.

sentences.zh: 蓋刑以禁亂，亂靜而刑息，不為承平設也。

translations.literal: Punishment exists to restrain disorder; when disorder is stilled, punishment ceases—it is not made for times of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment exists to restrain disorder; when disorder subsides, punishment should cease—it is not meant for peaceful times.

sentences.zh: 太平之人，樂德而惡刑，刑之所加，人必慘怛，故聖人貴措刑也。

translations.literal: Men in great peace delight in virtue and hate punishment; where punishment falls, men must grieve bitterly. Therefore the sage values easing punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In great peace men delight in virtue and loathe punishment; wherever punishment falls, men grieve bitterly. That is why the sage values easing punishment.

sentences.zh: 比大赦，澡蕩群罪，天下蒙慶，咸得自新。

translations.literal: Recently, in a great amnesty, all crimes were washed away; the realm received blessing and all could renew themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the recent great amnesty all crimes were washed away; the realm shared the blessing and every man could begin anew.

sentences.zh: 近日詔獄稍滋，鉤捕支黨，株蔓推窮，蓋獄吏不識天意，以抵慘刻。

translations.literal: Lately edicts on prisons have multiplied, associates are hooked and seized, roots and branches are pursued to the end—because prison officers do not understand Heaven's intent and meet harshness with harshness.
translations.idiomatic: Lately prison edicts have multiplied, associates are snared, and cases are pursued to the last branch—because jailers do not understand Heaven's intent and answer severity with severity.

sentences.zh: 誠宜廣愷悌之道，敕法慎罰，省白誣冤，此太平安人之務也。

translations.literal: Truly it is fitting to broaden the way of kindness and forbearance, restrain the law and be careful in punishment, and reduce false accusations and wrongful imprisonment—this is the task of great peace and the settling of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Truly the way of kindness and forbearance should be broadened, the law restrained, punishments applied with care, and false accusations reduced—this is the work of great peace and a settled people.

sentences.zh: 官人惟賢，政所以治也。

translations.literal: In appointing officials, only the worthy—thus is government ordered.
translations.idiomatic: In appointing officials, choose only the worthy—that is how government is ordered.

sentences.zh: 然君子小人各尚其類。

translations.literal: Yet the noble man and the petty man each honor their kind.
translations.idiomatic: Yet noble men and petty men each cleave to their own kind.

sentences.zh: 若陛下好賢而不任，任而不能信，信而不能終，終而不賞，雖有賢人，終不肯至，又不肯勸。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty loves the worthy yet does not employ them, employs yet cannot trust, trusts yet cannot see it through, sees it through yet does not reward—even with worthy men, in the end they will neither come nor exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty loves the worthy yet will not use them, uses them yet cannot trust them, trusts them yet cannot stay the course, and stays the course yet does not reward—even worthy men will neither come nor give their best.

sentences.zh: 反是，則天下之賢集矣。

translations.literal: Reverse this, and the worthy of the realm will gather.
translations.idiomatic: Reverse this, and worthy men throughout the realm will gather.

sentences.zh: 議者乃雲「賢不可知，人不易識」。

translations.literal: Critics then said, "The worthy cannot be known; men are not easy to recognize."
translations.idiomatic: Critics then said, "Talent cannot be known; men are hard to read."

sentences.zh: 臣以為固易知，固易識。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that they are indeed easy to know and indeed easy to recognize.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that they are in fact easy to know and easy to recognize.

sentences.zh: 夫尚德行者無兇險，務公正者無邪朋，廉者憎貪，信者疾偽，智不為愚者謀，勇不為怯者死，猶鸞隼不接翼，薰蕕不共氣，其理自然。

translations.literal: Those who honor virtue and conduct have no violence or treachery; those who pursue fairness and justice have no wicked factions; the incorruptible hate greed; the faithful hate falsehood; the wise do not plot for fools; the brave do not die for cowards—just as the luan and hawk do not fold wings together, and orchid and stenchweed do not share breath, so the principle is natural.
translations.idiomatic: Men who honor virtue and conduct are never violent or treacherous; men who pursue fairness have no wicked factions; the incorruptible despise greed; the faithful despise deceit; the wise do not scheme for fools; the brave do not die for cowards—just as luan birds and hawks do not fold wings together, and orchid and stenchweed do not share the same air, the principle is natural.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 以德並凶，勢不相入；

translations.literal: Virtue set beside violence—their forces cannot enter one another;
translations.idiomatic: Virtue placed beside violence—the two cannot mix;

sentences.zh: 以正攻佞，勢不相利；

translations.literal: uprightness attacking flattery—their forces cannot profit one another;
translations.idiomatic: uprightness set against flattery—the two cannot profit each other;

sentences.zh: 以廉勸貪，勢不相售；

translations.literal: incorruptibility urging greed—their forces cannot trade with one another;
translations.idiomatic: incorruptibility urging greed—the two cannot bargain together;

sentences.zh: 以信質偽，勢不相和。

translations.literal: faith questioning falsehood—their forces cannot harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: faith confronting falsehood—the two cannot harmonize.

sentences.zh: 智者尚謀，愚者所不聽；

translations.literal: The wise honor planning; fools will not listen;
translations.idiomatic: The wise live by counsel; fools will not heed it;

sentences.zh: 勇者徇死，怯者所不從。

translations.literal: the brave follow death; cowards will not follow.
translations.idiomatic: the brave follow death into battle; cowards will not follow.

sentences.zh: 此趣向之反也。

translations.literal: These inclinations are opposites.
translations.idiomatic: These inclinations stand directly opposed.

sentences.zh: 賢人未嘗不思效用，顧無其類則難進，是以湮汩于時。

translations.literal: Worthy men have never failed to think of serving effectively, but without their kind it is hard to advance, and so they are drowned in their time.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy men never cease wishing to serve, yet without their kind they cannot advance, and so they are lost in their age.

sentences.zh: 誠能信任俊良，知左右有灼然賢行者，賜之尊爵厚祿，使以類相舉，則天下之理得矣。

translations.literal: Truly, if you can trust outstanding men and know that among those at your side are plainly worthy in conduct, grant them high rank and generous salary and let them recommend their kind—then the principle of the realm is attained.
translations.idiomatic: Truly, if you trust outstanding men and recognize plainly worthy conduct among those at your side, grant them high rank and generous salary and let them recommend their kind—then the realm will be rightly ordered.

sentences.zh: 陛下知得賢須任，今未能者，蓋以常信任者不效。

translations.literal: Your Majesty knows that obtaining the worthy requires employment, yet today you cannot do so—presumably because those you have regularly trusted have not proved effective.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty knows that talent must be employed, yet today you cannot do so—presumably because those you have regularly trusted have failed you.

sentences.zh: 如裴炎、劉禕之、周思茂、騫味道固蒙用矣，皆孤恩前死，以是陛下疑于信賢。

translations.literal: Pei Yan, Liu Yizhi, Zhou Simao, and Qian Weidao were indeed employed, yet all died alone, stripped of favor beforehand—thus Your Majesty doubts trusting the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yan, Liu Yizhi, Zhou Simao, and Qian Weidao were indeed employed, yet all died forsaken and stripped of favor—thus Your Majesty doubts whether worthy men can be trusted.

sentences.zh: 臣固不然。

translations.literal: Your servant by no means thinks so.
translations.idiomatic: I do not agree.

sentences.zh: 昔人有以噎得病，乃欲絕食，不知食絕而身殞。

translations.literal: In former times a man choked while eating and then wished to stop eating altogether, not knowing that when eating ceased the body perished.
translations.idiomatic: Once a man choked while eating and wished to stop eating altogether, not knowing that when eating stops the body dies.

sentences.zh: 賢人于國，猶食在人，人不可以一噎而止餐，國不可以謬一賢而遠正士，此神鑒所知也。

translations.literal: Worthy men in the state are like food in a man: a man cannot stop eating because of one choke, and the state cannot cast off upright men because of one mistaken worthy—this Heaven's mirror knows.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy men in the state are like food in the body: one choke must not end all eating, and one mistaken appointment must not drive all upright men away—Heaven's mirror knows this.

sentences.zh: 聖人大德，在能納諫，太宗德參三王，而能容魏徵之直。

translations.literal: The sage's great virtue lies in being able to accept remonstrance. Emperor Taizong's virtue matched the Three Kings, and he could bear Wei Zheng's bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: The sage's great virtue lies in accepting remonstrance. Emperor Taizong's virtue matched the Three Sage-Kings, and he could bear Wei Zheng's blunt honesty.

sentences.zh: 今誠有敢諫骨鯁之臣，陛下廣延順納，以新盛德，則萬世有述。

translations.literal: Now, if there are truly ministers bold enough to remonstrate like a bone stuck in the throat, and Your Majesty broadly extends compliant acceptance to renew your flourishing virtue, then ten thousand generations will have something to tell.
translations.idiomatic: Now, if there truly are ministers bold enough to remonstrate like a bone in the throat, and Your Majesty welcomes their counsel to renew your flourishing virtue, then ten thousand generations will have your example to praise.

sentences.zh: 臣聞勞臣不賞，不可勸功；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when laboring ministers are not rewarded, merit cannot be encouraged;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when ministers who toil are not rewarded, merit cannot be encouraged;

sentences.zh: 死士不賞，不可勸勇。

translations.literal: If men who face death are not rewarded, one cannot encourage bravery.
translations.idiomatic: If those who die in service go unrewarded, there is no spurring men to valor.

sentences.zh: 今或勤勞死難，名爵不及；

translations.literal: Now some who toil and die in calamity receive no rank or title;
translations.idiomatic: Today some who labor until death in the state's service never receive rank or title;

sentences.zh: 偷榮屍祿，寵秩妄加，非所以表庸勵行者也。

translations.literal: while the idle enjoy glory and corpse-stained stipends, favor and ranks are recklessly bestowed—this is not the way to display merit and encourage right conduct.
translations.idiomatic: yet the undeserving hoard honor and draw salaries they never earned, while rank and favor are lavished without cause—hardly the way to honor merit and inspire right action.

sentences.zh: 願表顯徇節，勵勉百僚。

translations.literal: I pray that you make manifest those who gave their lives for principle, and encourage all officials.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that you publicly honor those who died upholding principle, and use their example to stir the whole bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 古之賞一人，千萬人悅者，蓋雲當也。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when one man was rewarded and ten thousand men rejoiced, it was presumably because the reward was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: In old times, when a single reward sent ten thousand hearts singing, it was because the honor was truly deserved.

sentences.zh: 今事之最大者，患兵甲歲興，賦役不省，興師十萬，則百萬之家不得安業。

translations.literal: Now the greatest matter is the worry that arms are raised year after year and levies and corvée are not reduced; when an army of a hundred thousand is mobilized, then a million households cannot keep to their occupations in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Of all pressing issues today, none match the annual call to arms and unrelenting levies: mobilize a hundred thousand troops, and a million homes lose their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 自有事北狄，於今十年，不聞中國之勝。

translations.literal: Since war with the northern barbarians began, ten years have passed to this day, yet no victory of the Middle Kingdom has been heard.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years now we have been at war with the northern tribes, yet not once have we heard of a Chinese victory.

sentences.zh: 以庸將禦冗兵，徭役日廣，兵甲日敝。

translations.literal: Mediocre generals command redundant troops; corvée grows daily wider, and armor and weapons daily more worn.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre commanders lead bloated armies; corvée grows heavier by the day, and weapons and armor more battered.

sentences.zh: 願審量損益，計利害，勢有不可，毋虛出兵，則人安矣。

translations.literal: I wish that you carefully weigh gain against loss and reckon profit against harm; where the situation forbids action, do not send troops in vain—then the people will be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh costs against benefits, measure harm against gain, and when the situation does not permit action, refrain from empty campaigns—then the people will know peace.

sentences.zh: 虺賊幹紀，自取屠滅，罪止魁逆，無復緣坐，宗室子弟，皆得更生。

translations.literal: The viper rebels violated the cosmic order and brought slaughter upon themselves; guilt rested only on the ringleaders and traitors, with no further guilt-by-association, and the sons and younger kinsmen of the imperial clan all regained new life.
translations.idiomatic: The serpent rebels defied heaven's order and brought destruction on themselves; punishment stopped with the ringleaders, collateral guilt was ended, and the younger members of the imperial clan were granted new life.

sentences.zh: 然臣願陛下重曉慰之，使明知天子慈仁，下得自安。

translations.literal: Yet I wish that Your Majesty would again make clear and comfort them, so that they plainly know the Son of Heaven's kindness and benevolence, and those below may find their own peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I beg Your Majesty to reassure them again, so they may know plainly the Son of Heaven's mercy—and find peace beneath it.

sentences.zh: 臣聞人情不能自明則疑，疑則懼，懼則罪生。

translations.literal: I have heard that when men's hearts cannot make themselves clear, then suspicion arises; with suspicion comes fear, and with fear comes the birth of guilt.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when people cannot clear their own names, suspicion follows; suspicion breeds fear, and fear begets crime.

sentences.zh: 惟賜愷悌之德，使居無過之地。

translations.literal: Only grant the virtue of kindness and forbearance, so that they may dwell in a place without fault.
translations.idiomatic: Grant them your kindness and forbearance, that they may live without reproach.

sentences.zh: 俄遷右衛胄曹參軍。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Army Aide in the Right Guard Rear-Office Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Army Aide in the Right Guard's Rear-Office Bureau.

sentences.zh: 後既稱皇帝，改號周，子昂上《周受命頌》以媚悅後。

translations.literal: After the Empress had styled herself Emperor and changed the dynastic title to Zhou, Zi'ang submitted "An Ode on Zhou's Receipt of the Mandate" to flatter and please the Empress.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress declared herself Emperor and changed the era name to Zhou, Zi'ang submitted An Ode on Zhou's Receipt of the Mandate to flatter her.

sentences.zh: 雖數召見問政事，論亦詳切，故奏聞輒罷。

translations.literal: Although he was repeatedly summoned to audience to discuss state affairs, and his discourse was also thorough and pointed, yet whenever he submitted a memorial and it was heard, it was always set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Though often summoned to discuss affairs of state—and though his counsel was thorough and pointed—every memorial he submitted was heard and then dismissed.

sentences.zh: 以母喪去官，服終，擢右拾遺。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he left office; when mourning ended, he was promoted to Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on his mother's death; when mourning ended, he was promoted to Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 子昂多病，居職不樂。

translations.literal: Zi'ang was often ill and took no joy in holding office.
translations.idiomatic: Zi'ang was chronically ill and found little satisfaction in his post.

sentences.zh: 會武攸宜討契丹，高置幕府，表子昂參謀。

translations.literal: It happened that Wu Youyi was dispatched to attack the Khitan; he lavishly staffed his headquarters, and submitted a memorial requesting Zi'ang as a staff adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Youyi was sent to campaign against the Khitan, he raised a grand headquarters staff and petitioned to have Zi'ang serve as adviser.

sentences.zh: 次漁陽，前軍敗，舉軍震恐，攸宜輕易無將略，子昂諫曰：「陛下發天下兵以屬大王，安危成敗在此舉，安可忽哉？」

translations.literal: When they reached Yuyang, the vanguard was defeated and the whole army trembled in terror; Youyi was frivolous and lacked a commander's strategy. Zi'ang remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty has dispatched the armies of the empire to the Great Prince; safety and peril, success and failure, hang on this single endeavor—how can it be treated lightly?"
translations.idiomatic: At Yuyang the vanguard was routed and the whole army shook with fear. Youyi was careless and lacked a commander's art. Zi'ang remonstrated: "Your Majesty has entrusted the armies of the empire to the Great Prince; safety and ruin, victory and defeat, all hang on this campaign—how can you treat it lightly?"

sentences.zh: 今大王法制不立，如小兒戲。

translations.literal: Now the Great Prince has not established military law—it is like child's play.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Great Prince has established no military discipline—it is child's play.

sentences.zh: 願審智愚，量勇怯，度眾寡，以長攻短，此刷恥之道也。

translations.literal: I pray that you examine wisdom and folly, measure courage and cowardice, and gauge numbers few and many, using strength against weakness—this is the way to wipe away shame.
translations.idiomatic: Discern the wise from the foolish, measure courage against cowardice, count numbers high and low, and strike with your strengths at their weaknesses—that is how shame is washed away.

sentences.zh: 夫按軍尚威嚴，擇親信以虞不測。

translations.literal: For indeed, in holding an army one honors awe and strictness, and selects trusted intimates to guard against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: An army demands awe and discipline; choose trusted men to guard against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 大王提重兵精甲，屯之境上，硃亥竊發之變，良可懼也。

translations.literal: The Great Prince holds heavy troops and fine armor, encamped on the frontier—a sudden blow like Zhu Hai's stealthy strike is truly to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Prince commands a heavy host in fine armor, encamped on the border—a stealthy blow like Zhu Hai's is truly to be feared.

sentences.zh: 王能聽愚計，分麾下萬人為前驅，契丹小丑，指日可擒。」

translations.literal: If the Prince will heed my humble plan, detach ten thousand men from under your command as vanguard—the Khitan, petty villains, can be captured within days."
translations.idiomatic: If you will hear my humble counsel, detach ten thousand of your men as vanguard—the Khitan rabble can be taken within days."

sentences.zh: 攸宜以其儒者，謝不納。

translations.literal: Youyi, taking him for a mere scholar, declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Youyi, dismissing him as a mere scholar, politely refused.

sentences.zh: 居數日，復進計，攸宜怒，徙署軍曹。

translations.literal: After several days he again advanced a plan; Youyi grew angry and transferred him to the post of Army Registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later he offered counsel again; Youyi grew angry and reassigned him to army registrar.

sentences.zh: 子昂知不合，不復言。

translations.literal: Zi'ang knew he was not compatible and spoke no more.
translations.idiomatic: Realizing he had no audience, Zi'ang said nothing more.

sentences.zh: 聖曆初，以父老，表解官歸侍，詔以官供養。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shengli era, because his father was aged, he submitted a memorial requesting to resign and return home to serve him; an edict ordered that his salary continue as support.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shengli, citing his father's age, he petitioned to resign and return home to care for him; the throne ordered his salary paid for his father's support.

sentences.zh: 會父喪，廬塚次，每哀慟，聞者為涕。

translations.literal: When his father died, he built a hut beside the tomb; each time he wailed in grief, those who heard wept.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he lived in a hut beside the tomb; his every cry of grief moved listeners to tears.

sentences.zh: 縣令段簡貪暴，聞其富，欲害子昂，家人納錢二十萬緡，簡薄其賂，捕送獄中。

translations.literal: The magistrate Duan Jian was greedy and brutal; hearing of Zi'ang's wealth, he wished to harm him. The family paid two hundred thousand strings of cash, but Jian thought the bribe too small and had him arrested and sent to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Duan Jian was greedy and violent; learning of Zi'ang's wealth, he sought to destroy him. The family paid two hundred thousand strings of cash, but Jian scorned the bribe as too small and had Zi'ang arrested and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 子昂之見捕，自筮，卦成，驚曰：「天命不祐，吾殆死乎！」

translations.literal: When Zi'ang was seized, he divined for himself; when the hexagram was complete, he cried in alarm: "Heaven's mandate does not protect me—I am perhaps about to die!"
translations.idiomatic: When Zi'ang was arrested, he cast a hexagram for himself; when it was complete, he cried in alarm: "Heaven does not protect me—I am surely about to die!"

sentences.zh: 果死獄中，年四十三。

translations.literal: And indeed he died in prison, aged forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He did die in prison, at forty-three.

sentences.zh: 子昂資褊躁，然輕財好施，篤朋友，與陸余慶、王無競、房融、崔泰之、盧藏用、趙元最厚。

translations.literal: By nature Zi'ang was narrow and quick-tempered, yet he was generous with wealth and loved to give, devoted to friendship; with Lu Yuqing, Wang Wujing, Fang Rong, Cui Taizhi, Lu Zangyong, and Zhao Yuan his bonds were deepest.
translations.idiomatic: Zi'ang was by nature narrow and impetuous, yet he cared little for money and loved to give; he was devoted to his friends, and closest of all to Lu Yuqing, Wang Wujing, Fang Rong, Cui Taizhi, Lu Zangyong, and Zhao Yuan.

sentences.zh: 唐興，文章承徐、庾餘風，天下祖尚，子昂始變雅正。

translations.literal: When Tang rose, literature still carried the afterwind of Xu and Yu; the realm took them as model and venerated them, and Zi'ang was the first to turn it toward elegance and rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tang founding, literature still breathed the lingering air of Xu Ling and Yu Xin; the realm looked to them as models—until Zi'ang turned the tide toward elegance and moral tone.

sentences.zh: 初，為《感遇詩》三十八章，王適曰：「是必為海內文宗。」

translations.literal: Early on, he composed thirty-eight chapters of "Poems on Encountering Fate"; Wang Shi said: "This man will surely become the literary patriarch within the seas."
translations.idiomatic: Early on he composed thirty-eight Poems on Encountering Fate; Wang Shi said, "This man will surely become the literary patriarch of the realm."

sentences.zh: 乃請交。

translations.literal: And thereupon asked to become his friend.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to become his friend.

sentences.zh: 子昂所論著，當世以為法。

translations.literal: What Zi'ang wrote and discoursed upon, the age took as standard.
translations.idiomatic: Zi'ang's essays and poems became the standard of his age.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，東川節度使李叔明為立旌德碑於梓州，而學堂至今猶存。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, the military commissioner of Dongchuan, Li Shuming, had an inscribed merit stele erected for him in Zizhou, and the school hall remains to this day.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era, Li Shuming, military commissioner of Dongchuan, erected a stele honoring his virtue in Zizhou; the school hall still stands today.

sentences.zh: 子光，復與趙元子少微相善，俱以文稱。

translations.literal: His son Zi Guang was also on good terms with Zhao Yuan and Zi Shaowei; all were famed for their writing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zi Guang was also close to Zhao Yuan and Zi Shaowei; all three were renowned for their writing.

sentences.zh: 光終商州刺史。

translations.literal: Guang ended his career as Prefect of Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guang eventually served as prefect of Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子易甫、簡甫，皆位御史。

translations.literal: His sons Yifu and Jianfu both reached the post of Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yifu and Jianfu both rose to be censors.

sentences.zh: 附 王無競王無競者，字仲烈，世徙東萊，宋太尉弘之遠裔。

translations.literal: Appendix: Wang Wujing. Wang Wujing, styled Zhonglie, for generations had moved to Donglai; a distant descendant of Grand Commandant Hong of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Wang Wujing. Wang Wujing, styled Zhonglie, came from a family long settled in Donglai, a distant scion of Grand Commandant Hong of Song.

sentences.zh: 家足於財，頗負氣豪縱。

translations.literal: The family was ample in wealth; he was quite proud in spirit, bold and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: The family was wealthy; he was proud-spirited, bold, and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 擢下筆成章科，調欒城尉，三遷監察御史，改殿中。

translations.literal: He was selected in the "Draft Prose at Will" examination, appointed Magistrate of Luancheng, thrice promoted to Investigating Censor, then transferred to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Draft Prose at Will examination, was posted as magistrate of Luancheng, was promoted three times to investigating censor, and then transferred to palace censor.

sentences.zh: 會朝，宰相宗楚客、楊再思離立偶語，無競揚笏曰：「朝禮上敬，公等大臣，不宜慢常典。」

translations.literal: At court audience, the chief ministers Zong Chuke and Yang Zaisi stood apart conversing casually; Wujing raised his court tablet and said: "In court ritual one honors what is above; you gentlemen are great ministers—you should not treat the regular statutes lightly."
translations.idiomatic: At court, chief ministers Zong Chuke and Yang Zaisi stood apart whispering together. Wujing raised his court tablet and said, "Court ritual demands reverence for what is above; you are great ministers—you should not treat the regular statutes lightly."

sentences.zh: 楚客怒，徙無競太子舍人。

translations.literal: Chuke grew angry and transferred Wujing to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke was angered and reassigned Wujing to attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，詆權幸，出為蘇州司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, he slandered the powerful favorites and was sent out as Vice-Prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shenlong era, he denounced the powerful favorites and was demoted to vice-prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 張易之等誅，坐嘗交往，貶廣州，仇家矯制搒殺之。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yizhi and the others were executed, he was implicated for having once associated with them, demoted to Guangzhou, and enemies forged an edict and beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Yizhi and his faction were executed, Wujing was punished for past association with them, exiled to Guangzhou, where enemies forged an imperial order and had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 附 趙元趙元，字貞固，河間人。

translations.literal: Appendix: Zhao Yuan. Zhao Yuan, styled Zhengue, was a native of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Zhao Yuan. Zhao Yuan, styled Zhengue, was from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 祖掞，號通儒，在隋，與同郡劉焯俱召至京師，補黎陽長，徙居汲。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shan was styled Tongru; under Sui, he and Liu Zhuo of the same commandery were both summoned to the capital, appointed Prefect of Liyang, and moved to settle in Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shan, known as the Comprehensive Scholar, served under the Sui; he and Liu Zhuo of the same commandery were summoned to the capital, appointed magistrate of Liyang, and later moved to Ji.

sentences.zh: 元少負志略，好論辯。

translations.literal: Yuan from youth possessed lofty resolve and strategy, and loved disputation.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yuan possessed lofty ambition and loved debate.

sentences.zh: 來游雒陽，士爭慕向，所以造謝皆縉紳選。

translations.literal: When he came to sojourn in Luoyang, scholars vied to admire and turn toward him; those who came to pay calls were all chosen men of the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: When he traveled to Luoyang, scholars vied to seek him out; every caller at his door was drawn from the finest of the gentry.

sentences.zh: 武后方稱制，懼不容其高，調宜祿尉。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu was just holding the regency, fearing she could not tolerate his eminence, he was appointed Magistrate of Yilu.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu had just seized power, fearing she could not brook his eminence, she posted him as magistrate of Yilu.

sentences.zh: 到職，非公事不言，彈琴蒔藥，如隱者之操。

translations.literal: On taking office, he spoke only on public business; he played the qin and tended medicinal herbs, like the conduct of a recluse.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he spoke only on official business; he played the zither and cultivated herbs, living like a hermit.

sentences.zh: 自傷位不配才，卒年四十九。

translations.literal: He grieved that his post did not match his talent, and died aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning that his rank did not match his gifts, he died at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 其友魏元忠、孟詵、宋之問、崔璩等共諡昭夷先生。

translations.literal: His friends Wei Yuanzhong, Meng Shen, Song Zhiwen, Cui Cong, and others together posthumously styled him Master Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: His friends Wei Yuanzhong, Meng Shen, Song Zhiwen, Cui Cong, and others jointly gave him the posthumous title Master Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：子昂說武后興明堂太學，其言甚高，殊可怪笑。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Zi'ang urged Empress Wu to raise the Bright Hall and Imperial Academy—his words were very lofty, and quite strange and laughable.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Zi'ang urged Empress Wu to build the Bright Hall and restore the Imperial Academy—his rhetoric soared high, which is both strange and absurd.

sentences.zh: 後竊威柄，誅大臣、宗室，肋逼長君而奪之權。

translations.literal: Later she stole the power of command, executed great ministers and the imperial clan, pressed upon the elder ruler's ribs and seized his authority.
translations.idiomatic: Later she seized power for herself, executed ministers and imperial kinsmen, and pressed the true sovereign aside to take his throne.

sentences.zh: 子昂乃以王者之術勉之，卒為婦人訕侮不用，可謂薦圭璧于房闥，以脂澤汙漫之也。

translations.literal: Zi'ang then urged her on with the arts of kingship, yet in the end was mocked and spurned as a woman would spurn him, unused—one might say offering jade scepters within the women's quarters, only to have them smeared with grease and rouge.
translations.idiomatic: Zi'ang counseled her with the arts of kingship, yet was mocked and ignored as a woman dismisses unwanted counsel—like offering jade scepters in the inner chambers only to have them smeared with cosmetics.

sentences.zh: 瞽者不見泰山，聾者不聞震霆，子昂之於言，其聾瞽歟。

translations.literal: The blind do not see Mount Tai; the deaf do not hear thunder—regarding speech, was Zi'ang deaf and blind?
translations.idiomatic: The blind cannot see Mount Tai; the deaf cannot hear thunder—for Zi'ang and his counsel, was he not deaf and blind?
